title: Blue Lies
affiliations: , University of Pennsylvania and Università degli Studi di Milano

detail.title: Blue Lies
detail.abstract: We introduce the “blue lies game,” a sender-receiver interaction where lying benefits both the liar and her ingroup member at the outgroup’s expense. Across 9,672 U.S. participants assigned to groups based on either random allocation or political partisanship, 38–57% of senders lie. An ingroup truth-telling norm reduces blue lies, but the same norm attributed to the outgroup has no effect or backfires among strong identifiers. Adding the option to remain silent cuts blue lies sharply and raises aggregate welfare. We structurally estimate via GMM a model that separates lying motives into monetary self-interest, ingroup loyalty, outgroup disregard, and honesty costs, and use it to quantify the welfare losses that blue lies impose. These findings have implications for understanding deception in polarized environments and designing interventions to reduce misinformation.

title: Does Voluntary Certification Promote Sustainability Investment?
affiliations: Wuhan University,  and Wuhan University

detail.title: Does Voluntary Certification Promote Sustainability Investment?
detail.abstract: Despite the prevalence of third-party sustainability certification, empirical evidence on whether such certification improves actual sustainability performance remains mixed. Motivated by this puzzle, we develop a game-theoretic model in which a firm chooses whether to make a costly sustainability investment and whether to pursue certification before selling in a regulated market. Consumers observe only price and certification status, but neither the firm's investment level nor its certification attempt. Certification plays two strategic roles: signaling sustainability to consumers and helping the firm mitigate regulatory risk before market entry. We show that lowering certification cost can either encourage or discourage investment. The latter occurs when regulation is sufficiently stringent: the firm may use certification as a substitute for investment, relying on its risk-mitigation effect rather than proactively improving sustainability. Our results suggest that policymakers carefully assess the joint impact of third-party certification and the regulatory environment. When regulation is already stringent, policymakers may achieve better outcomes by improving certification accuracy and consumer awareness than by reducing certification costs.

reference: CESifo Working Paper No. 12830
title: Taxing Wealth Unlocks Capital Gains: An Efficiency Rationale for Wealth Taxes
affiliations: University of Western Ontario, NHH Norwegian School of Economics - Department of Business and Management Science and NHH Norwegian School of Economics

detail.title: Taxing Wealth Unlocks Capital Gains: An Efficiency Rationale for Wealth Taxes
detail.abstract: Realization-based capital income taxation generates capital lock-in because investors have an incentive to delay tax payments. This generates inefficiency as investors forgo investment opportunities that require them to realize capital gains. We show that wealth taxation can unlock capital, eliminating the distortion on investors’ portfolio choice. Moreover, wealth taxes do not distort this choice in the absence of capital income taxation. This provides an efficiency rationale for wealth taxation independent of equity: shifting revenues from capital income to wealth taxes reduces distortions on portfolio choice. We provide conditions for the optimal tax mix between capital income and wealth taxes that balance the equity gains from both taxes against efficiency losses related to savings and portfolio choices. These conditions hinge on the cross-base elasticity of capital income to wealth taxes which captures lock-in responses.

reference: CESifo Working Paper No. 12828
title: Environmental Taxation and Financial Frictions in Green Lending
affiliations: and University of Bayreuth - Faculty of Law, Business and Economics

detail.title: Environmental Taxation and Financial Frictions in Green Lending
detail.abstract: We study polluting firms that require loans from a monopolistic bank to invest in abatement technology. Firms differ in the effectiveness of abatement investment, and this effectiveness is private information. The bank offers a screening contract under which high-cost firms receive too little capital and therefore emit excessively. A regulator restricted to tax policy responds by setting an environmental tax above marginal environmental damage, i.e., above the Pigouvian level. The first-best allocation can be restored by combining the Pigouvian tax, which ensures efficient abatement, with tailored, type-specific loan subsidies that correct the credit-market distortion.

title: Necro-Visibility: Platform Infrastructure, Communicative Enclosure, and the Structural Management of Political Testimony

detail.title: Necro-Visibility: Platform Infrastructure, Communicative Enclosure, and the Structural Management of Political Testimony
detail.abstract: This paper introduces necro-visibility, a concept developed to theorise a condition specific to the platform media era: the simultaneous unprecedented digital circulation of political testimony and its infrastructural containment in ways that structurally limit its translation into sustained political consequence. The concept emerges at the intersection of Achille Mbembe’s necropolitics, Judith Butler’s framework of grievability, Jodi Dean’s communicative capitalism, and the critical political economy of platform governance. It argues that necro-visibility is produced by the convergence of three structural conditions: a geopolitical or sociopolitical threat posed by the testimony to the power formation governing dominant platform infrastructure; a testimony density threshold sufficient to require targeted platform management; and the infrastructural deniability that distinguishes algorithmic governance from classical censorship. The primary empirical case is the Palestinian testimony ecosystem during Israel’s assault on Gaza from 2023 onward, anchored in the documented circulation and simultaneous suppression of Refaat Alareer’s poem If I Must Die. The paper develops a preliminary typology of visibility conditions, including full visibility with political consequence, necro-visibility, instrumentalised visibility, pre-testimonial erasure, domestic necro-visibility, and structural invisibility, to situate the paradigm case within a broader analytical spectrum. The paper extends beyond Kelly Lewis’s platform necropolitics by theorising the simultaneous amplification and containment of testimony through a single structural mechanism, the testimony commodity cycle, and introduces communicative enclosure as the structural precondition that determines in advance which populations’ testimony can exceed the threshold required for necro-visibility to operate.

title: The Niche as Necropolis: Capitalism, the Sub-Blogger, and the Death of the Symbolic Mother
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: The Niche as Necropolis: Capitalism, the Sub-Blogger, and the Death of the Symbolic Mother
detail.abstract: There is a particular kind of violence that announces itself as liberation, and the contemporary cult of "nishevost'" -- "nicheness," that untranslatable Russian-language term denoting the cultivated, marketable peculiarity of a personal brand -- is perhaps the purest specimen of this genre currently in circulation. The lecture series "Nishevost': kak kapitalizm nauchilsya prodavat' individual'nost'" (Nicheness: How Capitalism Learned to Sell Individuality), produced by the platform "Pravoye Polushariye Introverta" (The Introvert's Right Hemisphere), promises its viewers an answer to "how 'nicheness' makes everyone the same," framed explicitly against Thorstein Veblen's Theory of the Leisure Class and against the sociology of culture more broadly. The advertisement copy is a small masterpiece of unintentional irony: it sells, for free and without registration, a critique of the very mechanism by which it sells itself -- the cultivation of a niche audience (introverts, specifically, that most commodifiable of contemporary identities) through the promise of exclusive insight into how commodification works. This is not a contradiction so much as a structural truth laid bare: the critique of niche capitalism is itself the most lucrative niche available. Veblen (1899/2007) understood conspicuous consumption as a status game played by the leisure class to distinguish itself from labor; what the platform's blurb gestures toward, without quite arriving, is the inversion Veblen could not have anticipated -- a status game in which the commodity being conspicuously consumed is not a top hat or a yacht but the buyer's own unrepeatable interior life, hawked back to her in the form of a Telegram channel subscription.

title: The Tamagotchi Economy: Niche, Lipstick, and the Gendered Spectacle of Post-Soviet Platform Capitalism
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: The Tamagotchi Economy: Niche, Lipstick, and the Gendered Spectacle of Post-Soviet Platform Capitalism
detail.abstract: Somewhere between a TikTok ring light and a Telegram paywall, a new anthropological subject has crystallized: the woman who pays a stranger forty dollars a month for the privilege of watching her buy a handbag. She is not deceived. She knows the blogger is not her friend. She knows the "personal growth" coaching call is dramaturgy, that the tearful confession on a Zoom screen is blocked out like a soap opera beat, that the influencer's villa in five hundred near-identical Reels is rented for the afternoon. And she pays anyway — not despite the fiction, but because of it. This essay begins from that paradox, because it is the paradox on which an entire economy now runs: an economy of niches, lipsticks, tamagotchis, and borrowed children, in which capitalism has discovered that the most profitable commodity left to sell is the self, packaged, narrated, and sold back to its owner in dazzling, deniable fragments. The five fragments of vernacular cultural criticism that occasion this essay — circulating, as such things now do, as Telegram chat logs, half-finished video essays, and recession-economics trivia — describe what looks, at first glance, like five unrelated phenomena. There is the "lipstick index," the durable folk-economic claim that cosmetics sales rise in a recession. There is the cult of "nicheness," the contemporary mania for curating an identity so particular that mass culture cannot touch it. There is the blogger as "tamagotchi," the paid intimacy economy in which a poor subscriber buys five vicarious lives from a rich one. There is "Kaptsova," a composite figure for the female life-coach-cum-romance-simulator who monetizes loneliness through Zoom calls that blur coaching, therapy, and webcam intimacy, sometimes with an undertow of submission and humiliation. And there is the unnamed "sugar mommy," the woman who satisfies a narcissistic and quasi-maternal hunger by lavishing status goods on someone else's child, all while society reserves its moral alarm for men. I will argue across the length of this essay that these are not five phenomena but one: a single libidinal-economic structure in which the gendered self is dismantled into purchasable units of attention, taste, intimacy, and care, and reassembled as a product line.

reference: CESifo Working Paper No. 12826
title: Growth and Debt Sustainability Trade-offs in the Presence of Climate Shocks and Uncertainties
affiliations: , World Bank, World Bank and World Bank

detail.title: Growth and Debt Sustainability Trade-offs in the Presence of Climate Shocks and Uncertainties
detail.abstract: Climate shocks create a difficult policy problem: an intervention that protects growth can also strain public finances, and these trade-offs are magnified by uncertainty about both the shocks themselves and the macroeconomic model used to assess them. In this paper, a methodology to explore these issues is presented and applied to the management of coastal flood risks in the Maldives. The analysis uses a version of the World Bank MFMod macrostructural model that includes stochastic damages from coastal flood and model uncertainty. It evaluates two policy options (prevention and preparedness) using three metrics: expected GDP losses, the probability that debt exceeds a sustainability threshold, and the probability of a sharp deterioration in the debt ratio. Results show that climate risks are macro-critical in the Maldives and that individual policies create synergies and trade-offs. Investments in prevention are win-win, with gains in GDP enhancing debt sustainability, but only up to a certain level. Beyond a threshold, there is a trade-off between growth and debt sustainability as debt-financed prevention investments worsen debt vulnerabilities in spite of the GDP gains they generate. Preparedness alone (through contingency funds or other instruments) improves fiscal resilience, especially in context of large tail risks. Policy mixes mitigate trade-offs and preparedness and prevention are complement: preparedness enables larger prevention investments without magnifying debt vulnerability, leading to larger GDP gains. Introducing model uncertainty widens the distribution of possible outcomes but does not affect key policy conclusions. The main policy message is that robust climate macrofiscal planning should move beyond expected values and focus on policy mixes that combine prevention and preparedness to manage growth and debt sustainability across a wide range of plausible futures.

reference: CESifo Working Paper No. 12829
title: Machine Learning and Liquidity Dynamics in European Stock Markets
affiliations: Council of Economic Advisors, Ministry of Finance, Hellenic Republic, Brunel University London - Department of Economics and Finance and

detail.title: Machine Learning and Liquidity Dynamics in European Stock Markets
detail.abstract: This paper examines the forecasting of liquidity dynamics in European stock markets by means of traditional econometric models and machine learning techniques. It uses daily data for the DAX, CAC 40, FTSE 100, FTSE MIB, and IBEX 35 over 2010–2026, liquidity being measured by the logarithmic Amihud illiquidity indicator. The empirical framework compares ARIMA models and a dynamic panel specification with Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Support Vector Regression (SVR) within a common rolling one-step-ahead forecasting framework. The results show that liquidity is highly persistent and that the dynamic panel model achieves the lowest forecast errors, although Diebold–Mariano tests indicate no significant predictive advantage over the leading machine learning models. SHAP analysis reveals that trading activity, lagged liquidity, and market uncertainty are the main determinants of liquidity forecasts. The findings highlight the complementary role of explainable machine learning in empirical finance.

title: When Regulators Overlap: Fragmented Regulation and Corporate Environmental Footprints
affiliations: Northern Trust Corporation - Northern Trust Asset Management, Vietnam National University - Ho Chi Minh City (VNU-HCM), University of Economics Ho Chi Minh City and Griffith University - Griffith Business School

detail.title: When Regulators Overlap: Fragmented Regulation and Corporate Environmental Footprints
detail.abstract: This paper examines whether regulatory fragmentation affects corporate carbon emissions. Using U.S firms from 2003 to 2023, this paper confirms that firms exposed to greater fragmentation across federal regulators generate higher carbon emissions. The effect is economically meaningful and robust across a battery of robustness checks. We further show that regulatory fragmentation operates through weakened corporate carbon reduction initiatives, including emission-reduction policies and targets. The effect is weaker when firms have stronger sustainability governance and external monitoring. Overall, the findings reveal an unintended carbon cost of fragmented regulatory oversight.

detail.abstract: Prediction markets aggregate dispersed information into probabilistic forecasts that consistently outperform polls and expert panels, yet their adoption is constrained by a structural liquidity problem: providers of market depth bear adverse selection risk that deters retail participation. We present the Onix Protocol, a hybrid architecture that decouples the pricing function from the settlement function in prediction markets. By pairing automated market maker pricing-a Constant Product Market Maker (CPMM) for binary outcomes and a Logarithmic Market Scoring Rule (LMSR) for multi-outcome markets-with parimutuel (totalizator) settlement, we achieve a structural guarantee that liquidity-provider principal is never at risk from betting outcomes. We formalize the protocol's economic invariants, prove the LP principal guarantee for both market types, describe a "Lazy" liquidity pool enabling passive retail participation, analyze the dispute resolution mechanism under DAO governance, and discuss the experimental hypotheses this system is designed to test. The protocol is implemented as consensus-level operations on the VIZ distributed ledger.

title: The Forgotten Core of the Father of Strategic Management: Revisiting the Ansoff-Mintzberg Debate and the Strategic Success Hypothesis Purpose
affiliations: Ca Foscari University of Venice, Department of Management, Students

detail.title: The Forgotten Core of the Father of Strategic Management: Revisiting the Ansoff-Mintzberg Debate and the Strategic Success Hypothesis Purpose
detail.abstract: This paper reconstructs the Ansoff-Mintzberg exchange as a historically significant contingency truce rather than a winner-loser outcome. It argues that the debate's enduring legacy is the unresolved question of strategic correctness: when firms should converge toward prevailing industry norms and when they should diverge in pursuit of strategic becoming. From this perspective, the paper repositions Igor Ansoff as a pioneer whose most consequential contribution-the Strategic Success Hypothesis (SSH)-was gradually marginalized, fragmented in later research and left only partially validated for decades.

title: The Role of Arrival-Rate Uncertainty in Priority Queues
affiliations: , Hebrew University of Jerusalem and Hebrew University of Jerusalem

detail.title: The Role of Arrival-Rate Uncertainty in Priority Queues
detail.abstract: We study priority pricing in an unobservable single-server queue when customers commit to purchasing priority before the arrival rate is revealed. Because a customer is more likely to arrive when the arrival rate is high, fully rational customers assign greater weight to higharrival-rate realizations, whereas naive customers continue to use the prior distribution. Since the value of priority increases with congestion, naive customers systematically underestimate that value and consequently have a lower willingness to pay. We show that this belief distortion determines the value of pricing flexibility. A fixed price is simple to implement, but may leave customers paying more for priority than the reduction in waiting costs it ultimately provides, an outcome we refer to as ex-post regret. It also generates lower revenue when customers are naive. Rate-contingent pricing provides a robust benchmark that eliminates regret and is unaffected by the customers' rationality level. More aggressive rate-contingent pricing can extract additional revenue from naive customers, but sacrifices robustness and may increase regret. A full refund policy also eliminates regret, but at a revenue cost. The analysis reveals a trade-off between revenue extraction, robustness, customer regret, and implementation simplicity under arrival-rate uncertainty.

title: Saturation Room and Firm Value: A Valuation Framework for AI-Native Firms

detail.title: Saturation Room and Firm Value: A Valuation Framework for AI-Native Firms

detail.abstract: Building on the saturation-decoupling theorem of Paper I, this paper addresses a valuation question: when a firm's value comes from unrealized saturation room—the gap between coverage x and its ceiling x̄—rather than from current cash flow, how should it be valued? Our central result is a misspecification-cost theorem (Proposition 1): any valuation that extrapolates from observed cash flow without explicitly modeling the coverage path x → x̄ underestimates such firms by an amount that is strictly positive and increases monotonically in the distance to saturation; a correctly specified path-forecasting valuation recovers true value exactly. The underestimation is therefore not a property of discounting but of anchoring. We then define FACE, a valuation re-anchored on net-worth accumulation (N, assets minus liabilities on a non-monetary balance sheet), and prove a consistency result (Proposition 3): under a stated parameterization the FACE compounding form agrees with true value to first order, with its gap from cash-flow-anchored DCF equal to the present value of saturation room. Finally, we derive the value–cash-flow lead–lag from an explicit two-rate dynamical system in which execution accumulates exponentially while monetization relaxes toward an Amdahl ceiling at a bandwidth-limited rate; the lead is obtained in closed form and is positive exactly when judgment bandwidth binds (Proposition 4). This is pure theory; we report no empirics but provide a refutable interface with operational proxies.

title: Powertrain Portfolio Under Discrete Choice Model: A Deep Reinforce Learning Method
affiliations: Tianjin University of Finance and Economics, Tianjin University of Finance and Economics, Tianjin University of Finance & Economics and Tianjin University of Finance and Economics

detail.title: Powertrain Portfolio Under Discrete Choice Model: A Deep Reinforce Learning Method
detail.abstract: This paper examines strategic powertrain transition and compliance management under China's Dual-Credit Policy, characterized by endogenous demand-technology-regulation co-evolution. We formulate a Markov Decision Process (MDP) framework with Multinomial Logit (MNL) demand to jointly optimize RD investment, pricing, and compliance credit trading and banking decisions across diverse new energy vehicle (NEV) and conventional fuel vehicle (CFV) offerings. Since high-dimensional continuous states and nonlinear MNL choice probabilities preclude closed-form solutions, we develop a CSAC-DualCredit algorithm as the solver. Findings show that: (1) electric range amplifies while conventional fuel vehicle fuel consumption attenuates profit sensitivity to credit prices; (2) optimal pricing favors NEVs only when consumer price sensitivity exceeds a threshold, reflecting underlying technological diversity; and (3) the algorithm guarantees feasibility without sacrificing exploration. Numerical results offer actionable strategies for navigating coupled transitions under volatile regulations.

title: 'Capital' and 'Current' Account Dimensions of Financial Sanctions
affiliations: International Monetary Fund (IMF) - Legal Department and HEC Paris

detail.title: 'Capital' and 'Current' Account Dimensions of Financial Sanctions
detail.abstract: This article analyses the international legal framework governing financial sanctions, with particular emphasis on the distinction between current and capital account transactions. It examines how cross-border financial flows affected by sanctions are regulated under three principal regimes: the IMF Articles of Agreement, WTO law, and international investment agreements. The analysis shows that these frameworks provide differing and partly overlapping forms of legal coverage, resulting in an uneven and segmented regulatory landscape. While restrictions on payments and transfers relating to current transactions are generally subject to more developed legal disciplines, capital movements are regulated in a more limited and differentiated manner across the regimes. The article further considers how the classification of a measure as affecting current or capital transactions influences its legal treatment and the extent of applicable obligations. It argues that this classification is central to understanding the legal reach of financial sanctions. In addition, it reviews the role of security exceptions, which are present across all three frameworks and significantly affect the degree to which financial sanctions are subject to international scrutiny and review.

title: Multi-Round Broadcast Matching
affiliations: Cornell University - Operations Research and Industrial Engineering, Cornell University - Operations Research and Industrial Engineering and Cornell University - School of Operations Research and Information Engineering

detail.title: Multi-Round Broadcast Matching
detail.abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of designing broadcast sets in real time and formulate a multi-round stochastic broadcast matching model with a uniform lottery allocation rule, under which an order that receives multiple acceptances is assigned uniformly at random among the accepting drivers. We formulate linear programming relaxations that upper bound the expected reward of any adaptive policy and develop an LP-based randomized algorithm for the resulting dynamic broadcast matching problem. A key challenge, absent from standard one-to-one dispatch and sequential probing models, is that removing unavailable drivers alters competition for orders and can inflate conditional matching probabilities under uniform lottery allocation. We overcome this challenge and establish approximation ratios of (1-e-2)/2 ≈ 0.43 for the single-order setting and (1-e-3)/3 ≈ 0.32 for the general multiple-order setting. We further provide matching upper-bound instances establishing the tightness of our approximation ratio in the multiple-order setting. Finally, we develop an efficient column-generation framework for solving the LP, and our numerical results show that our algorithm performs well compared against one-to-one dispatch baselines.

title: Strategic Responses to Non-Market Risks and Capability Building of EMNEs: A Multi-case Study of Chinese Firms in the US Market

detail.title: Strategic Responses to Non-Market Risks and Capability Building of EMNEs: A Multi-case Study of Chinese Firms in the US Market

declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported by JSPS KAKENHI (Grant Number 22K13480).

detail.abstract: This study examines how emerging market multinational enterprises (EMNEs) respond to non-market risks in developed host countries to overcome the Liability of Origin (LoO). Integrating institutional theory, the legitimacy-based view of political risk, non-market strategy, and EMNE capability theory, the study derives five propositions and assesses them through a multi-case study of three Chinese technology firms, Huawei, DJI, and TikTok (ByteDance), facing U.S. government sanctions. The findings indicate that EMNE resilience under acute geopolitical risk rests on the combination of autonomous, irreplaceable product value and structural reconfiguration at the parent level, rather than on the avoidance-oriented strategies predicted by conventional institutional and corporate political activity theory. Product value functions as a societal legitimacy shield only when it is not dependent on inputs controlled by the sanctioning government, a boundary condition that explains the divergence in market outcomes across the three cases. The study contributes to the literature on non-market strategy, the LoO, the advantage of emergingness, and de-globalization.

title: Japanese FX intervention in 2026
affiliations: Kobe City University of Foreign Studies and Kobe City University of Foreign Studies

detail.title: Japanese FX intervention in 2026

detail.abstract: This paper examines the effectiveness of Japanese foreign exchange (FX) intervention implemented in late April and early May 2026. Employing synthetic control methods to construct counterfactual exchange rate paths, we find that the effect of this yen-buying intervention event remained statistically significant for five business days after the end of the intervention. Comparing this event with the FX intervention events in 2022-24, we show that the power of the lasting effect for the recent intervention event was substantially weaker than those for the events of October 21 and 24, 2022, April 29 and May 1, 2024, and July 11 and 12, 2024. Consequently, our findings demonstrate that despite implementing large-scale yen-buying interventions totaling approximately 12 trillion yen, the spring 2026 intervention event yielded limited effectiveness. This attenuated lasting effect could stem from the widening of the US-Japan interest rate differential following the intervention.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a static theoretical model of electric vehicle (EV) adoption and compares firms in two economies. Economy H has high financial constraints due to high interest rate and a tight borrowing cap while Economy L has a lower interest rate and a comparatively relaxed borrowing cap, both with a single profit maximizing small and medium enterprise each. Using Lagrangian optimisation with Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions, three results are derived. First, the borrowing cap determines level of EV adoption. Firm in economy L achieves a higher EV adoption level when the borrowing constraint binds. Second, when the borrowing constraint binds, the borrowing cap is the sole determinant of EV adoption, while the interest rate affects profitability but not adoption quantity. Third, comparative statics confirm that a higher interest rate reduces EV adoption level and a higher borrowing cap raises EV adoption at a diminishing rate.

title: Bank Specialization and SMEs' Employment Stability
affiliations: , Universite de Limoges, LAPE, Université de Limoges, LAPE and Université de Limoges, LAPE

detail.title: Bank Specialization and SMEs' Employment Stability
detail.abstract: Using proprietary data from Banque de France, we show that banks' geographic and industry specialization help stabilize SMEs' employment during adverse sales shocks, particularly when these shocks are transitory. Also, specialized banks absorb the cost of adverse sales shocks, opposing the flight-to-productivity argument. Mechanism analysis reveals that specialization alleviates SMEs' financial constraints during downturns, providing the liquidity necessary to support labor hoarding. Also, the direct employment-stabilizing effect of bank specialization is distinct from relationship lending. Our identification isolates firm-specific sales shocks by benchmarking firms' sales growth against industry levels and uses the heterogeneity in the EU crisis's severity across industries as a source of exogeneity. Our findings suggest that specialized banks act as providers of liquidity insurance, enabling SMEs to honor implicit labor agreements during short-term sales downturns.

title: Psychological Alignment Framework: Evaluating Workplace Alignment and Its Impact on Organizational Outcomes

detail.abstract: In today’s increasingly competitive and evolving business world, corporations face growing challenges in maintaining high levels of performance while being able to adequately address the psychological needs of their employees. This study examines how organizations can better align with business objectives with employee expectations to create more effective, sustainable, and productive workplace environments. This research introduces a Psychological Alignment Framework (PAF) which explores the relationship between workplace conditions and key employee outcomes such as engagement, retention, performance, and satisfaction. A mixed-method approach was used, incorporating both qualitative interviews and quantitative survey data collected from individuals entering or currently in the workforce as well as those who’ve had extensive careers to see expectations from the top-down. An inductive approach was applied to develop the framework, with responses analyzed through indicators such as frequency, intensity, and consistency. The findings indicate that domains such as Trust and Psychological Safety and Connection and Belonging serve as primary drivers of positive employee outcomes, while Agency and Empowerment were shown to support long-term engagement and growth. Purpose Alignment, although deemed important, demonstrated variability in its direct impact on behavior and productivity. Overall, the study highlights that integrating psychological considerations into organizational practices is essential for improving both employee experience and overall organizational effectiveness.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence is moving past a critical threshold: from systems that generate outputs to systems that carry out actions. Agentic AI systems reason, plan, make decisions, invoke tools, execute transactions, and collaborate with other agents to advance goals on behalf of individuals and organisations. That transition changes what governance must actually scrutinise. The pertinent question is no longer whether a model's output is accurate, but whether a system's action is authorised, constrained, reversible, observable, and accountable. This paper contends that the shift is one of kind rather than degree, and that it justifies a discipline of its own: we name that discipline Agentic AI Governance-the governance of machine agency rather than machine intelligence. Extending, rather than supplanting, established instruments such as the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, ISO/IEC 42001, the EU AI Act, and Singapore's Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI, the paper advances five contributions. First, it frames machine agency as the object of governance and sets out why agentic systems are categorically distinct from traditional AI, generative AI, deterministic automation, and engineered autonomous systems. Second, it surfaces the structural assumptions that lead existing frameworks to undergovern agentic systems. Third, it introduces a six-class Agentic AI Risk Taxonomy covering agency, operational, regulatory, security, multi-agent, and accountability risks. Fourth, it puts forward the Agentic AI Governance Discipline and Operating Model (AAGDOM)-five interlocking pillars (Human Oversight; Authority & Delegation; Risk Management; Accountability; Runtime Controls) made operational through a lifecycle operating model and an Agent Registry. Fifth, it presents an Agentic Governance Maturity Model that lets enterprises benchmark and advance their capability. Taken together, these provide a coherent, adoptable foundation for deploying autonomous agents in regulated settings with justified confidence.

title: Can LLMs Perform Geospatial Reasoning? A Case Study for Congestion Pricing in New York City

detail.title: Can LLMs Perform Geospatial Reasoning? A Case Study for Congestion Pricing in New York City
detail.abstract: This study evaluates the geospatial reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) using New York City's Congestion Pricing Program as a case study. We benchmark four representative models (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and Qwen) on taxi-trip toll prediction under progressively richer geographic and policy inputs. The results show substantial variation between both models and the input settings. Structured location metadata provides the most reliable grounding, while excessive or redundant geographic context can introduce instability. Error analysis reveals recurring failures in temporal-policy reasoning and model-specific biases. In general, LLMs can help interpret geospatial policies when properly grounded, but they remain unsuitable as standalone, deterministic systems for enforcing transportation policies.

title: The Corporate Villainy of Tom Sawyer: Manufactured Scarcity, the Ethics of Attention, and the Literary Prehistory of Dark Patterns

detail.title: The Corporate Villainy of Tom Sawyer: Manufactured Scarcity, the Ethics of Attention, and the Literary Prehistory of Dark Patterns
detail.abstract: The whitewashing scene in Mark Twain's The Adventures of Tom Sawyer (1876) is conventionally received in one of two ways: as a comic illustration of the malleability of value, the reading made canonical in behavioral economics by Ariely, Loewenstein, and Prelec (2006), or as a celebration of the boyish individualist, the reading carried into popular culture by works such as Rush's 1981 song of the same name. This paper proposes a third reading. It argues that the scene is the earliest structurally complete literary rendering of the design logic now catalogued under the heading of dark patterns: manufactured scarcity, engineered desire, and the extraction of value from a manipulated audience. On this reading Tom is not a charming rascal but the prototype of the engagement designer who optimizes a system against the people inside it. The paper distinguishes two ethics of gamification, the earned, in which an activity is genuinely made worth doing and the designer participates in it, and the engineered, in which desire for access to a hollow good is manufactured and the designer abstains, and it proposes the designer's own abstention, the refusal to consume the product, as a diagnostic of the engineered kind. Locating the reading within the ethics of attention and persuasive design (Fogg, 2003; Verbeek, 2011; Williams, 2018) and the dark patterns literature (Brignull, 2010; Mathur et al., 2019), it contends that the fence is not a quaint antecedent but a working model of contemporary attention capture, and that the uniformly admiring reception of Tom is itself evidence of how thoroughly the culture has naturalized the extractor as hero. It closes on the irony that Twain, who coined the term Gilded Age and named the capitalist as the oppressor, narrated the con as cleverness and never marked it as harm.

detail.abstract: Generative AI is a prominent example of a broader challenge firms face when adopting new technologies: their benefits are often uneven across tasks and workers, exhibiting a "jagged technological frontier." We study whether managers anticipate that the benefits of new technologies are uneven across tasks and workers, and how the information environment affects deployment. In a linked worker-manager experiment, workers complete real-effort tasks with and without generative AI, allowing us to estimate AI effects by task and worker type. Managers then predict AI-assisted performance and make incentivized deployment decisions. Without feedback, most managers mistakenly expect AI to improve performance on both sides of the frontier. Performance feedback reduces average optimism, but substantial overestimation remains for outside-frontier tasks. We further examine incentive-compatible deployment decisions for two new tasks (one inside and one outside the frontier). Managers' willingness to pay (WTP) is high across all tasks, and even higher for the outside-frontier task where AI does not add value. An information-design intervention in the Feedback condition that makes salient which tasks are inside or outside the frontier reduces WTP for outside-frontier deployment relative to inside-frontier deployment. This evidence is consistent with salience-based memory retrieval: the negative effects of AI are only corrected when the boundaries of the technology are made salient. The findings suggest that realizing organizational gains from new technologies depends not only on technical capability, but on information environments that make the limits of those capabilities visible to decision-makers.

detail.abstract: Run charts are a foundational tool in healthcare quality improvement, used to detect non-random signals of process change through four established rules: shift, trend, unusual number of runs, and the astronomical data point. Of these, only the astronomical point rule lacks a probability-based or otherwise quantitative definition; its originators explicitly describe it as a subjective, visual judgment. This inconsistency undermines the reproducibility that quality systems are meant to guarantee: a system, by definition, should produce uniform output regardless of who applies it. This paper proposes a simple correction, the Objective Astronomical Point Rule (OAPR, informally the "Baqir Rule"): every run chart used for quality monitoring should be accompanied by a boxplot of the same dataset, with outlier status determined using Tukey's interquartile range (IQR) method (a point falling below Q1-1.5×IQR or above Q3 + 1.5×IQR) rather than by unaided visual inspection. This replaces a subjective judgment with a fixed, auditable, and repeatable statistical test, aligning the astronomical point rule with the objectivity already present in the other three run chart rules.

detail.abstract: For more than two decades the Net Promoter Score (NPS) has served as the single number boards trust to summarize customer advocacy, earning that standing not through psychometric strength but through a structural property: it compresses advocacy into one comparable figure that measures whether one human will recommend a brand to another. That premise is now incomplete. As AI agents assume the shopper function, the entity that asks on a buyer's behalf is increasingly an algorithm rather than a friend, and the recommendation that decides a purchase is increasingly the agent's. This is the problem the present paper addresses: the boardroom's headline advocacy number no longer measures the channel where purchase decisions are now being made. The contribution is the Algorithmic NPS, also termed the Agentic NPS: the agent-side counterpart to the Net Promoter Score, computed on the same minus-100 to plus-100 scale, that measures whether an AI agent surfaces, ranks, and recommends a focal entity when it answers a shopper's query. We define four agent-response classes (Promoter, Passive, Detractor, and a fourth that has no analogue in survey-based measurement, Absent), argue that Absent should count on the Detractor side because in agent-mediated discovery invisibility is the modal and most damaging outcome, name the distance between a firm's Human NPS and its Algorithmic NPS the ANPS Gap, and specify the unit of analysis as the storefront entity identified by its registered domain. Measurement of whether an AI system surfaces a brand is not itself new; a commercial category of AI-visibility and generative-engine-optimization analytics already reports presence, mention rate, and ranking position. The contribution is the join the surrounding literatures leave open: an advocacy number on the Net Promoter scale, the treatment of non-mention as a Detractor-side outcome, and the cross-instrument Gap against the firm's Human NPS. In scope, the construct is confined to two actors and is reported as one number per actor, mapped to the decision that actor fights to win, so that a brand's Algorithmic NPS measures what to buy and a retailer's measures where to buy. We advance five testable propositions and illustrate the construct with a single anonymized European appliance-retail cohort that exhibits a large discovery-versus-transaction spread. This is a conceptual working paper introducing and defining a construct; it does not present a validated instrument.

title: The Dimensionality Ceiling: Cross-Domain Synthesis and the Recognition of Value
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: The Dimensionality Ceiling: Cross-Domain Synthesis and the Recognition of Value
detail.abstract: As language models absorb more of the human record, this paper asks where their reach ends and answers with a falsifiable conjecture: a measurable ceiling on what a corpusbound system can recognise as worth pursuing, graded by how far across knowledge a synthesis reaches. Generating connections across fields is cheap, and models can produce arrangements in no single source; what stays hard is recognising which is valuable, the judgement that turns reach into use. The standard by which an unprecedented synthesis is judged worthwhile is not yet in the record that the model and any learned evaluator are made from, so recognition at the frontier cannot be read off the corpus, and does not get cheap as generation does. The limit is jagged, not uniform, and tightens with reach: the writing that would value a distant connection is produced by the same rare authors who would draw the bridge, and goes missing with it. The paper calls this reach-graded surface the dimensionality ceiling. It separates three senses in which a bridge can be missing, only one of which is the durable human locus, and places the residue where no automatic test can settle worth. The conjecture is falsifiable, and the test that could overturn it doubles as a map of where human synthesis still matters most. That map, not a forecast about wages, scale, or employment, is the societal stake this paper presses; the labour-market questions stay separate.

detail.abstract: This study examines the behavioural drivers of Generation Z purchasing decisions in England and explores their implications for AI-driven cross-selling systems in the fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) sector. Using a quantitative cross-sectional survey (n = 54), data were analysed using SPSS 28 to assess the influence of key behavioural constructs, including social media engagement, platform preference, ethical considerations, social visibility, and digital payment adoption. The findings indicate that social media engagement and e-payment systems are significant drivers of purchasing behaviour, while demographic variables demonstrate limited explanatory power. Reliability analysis reveals variation across constructs, highlighting the complexity of operationalising emerging consumer behaviours within digitally mediated environments. Positioned as exploratory and hypothesis-generating, the study proposes a novel framework integrating behavioural segmentation, platform-specific engagement, ethical positioning, and mobile-first purchasing systems. The research contributes to the growing literature on digitally mediated consumer decision-making and offers foundational insights for the development of AI-driven recommendation and cross-selling systems.

detail.abstract: Does market concentration have a "natural ceiling" from the demand side? Industrial Organization economics, since Bain (1956), has measured "how concentrated" markets are using indicators such as CR4 and HHI, but has never systematically answered "how concentrated they should be." This paper proposes a theory of market structure boundaries grounded in demand-side cognitive architecture. The core argument is as follows: in any market, the decision-maker's cognitive system can seriously process only a limited number of equivalent options at any given moment. This capacity ceiling—termed the Cognitive Pool with depth N—constitutes a structural boundary on market concentration, namely the Cognitive Ceiling: CR1* = 1/N. When the largest participant breaches this ceiling in actual market share, a qualitative transition occurs in demand-side decision modes: from "oscillating and comparing" among options to "no longer comparing, merely following the market leader." This paper constructs a two-layer ceiling with a complete dynamic cycle, proposes an Active Market/Cold Market/Crossing Market trichotomy, argues for the possibility of the Sustained Titan, and provides six testable empirical propositions. In the empirical portion, rollback validation is conducted on 15 cases from Western and comparative markets. Across 48 historical validation time points, the diagnostic protocol achieves a directional accuracy of 93.8%. The Ω toolkit's incremental value over HHI lies in explanatory power—distinguishing inertial zombies, scarcity-driven expansion, firm decline, category erosion, and pre-awakening organizational mutation.

title: Artificial General Intelligence as a General-Purpose Technology: Toward an AGI-Augmented Theory of Economic Growth

detail.title: Artificial General Intelligence as a General-Purpose Technology: Toward an AGI-Augmented Theory of Economic Growth

detail.abstract: Korinek (2024) models AGI as an augmentation of labor in the production function Y t = A t F (K t , L t +M t). In a telling footnote he acknowledges that "a more comprehensive production function under AGI could distinguish labor into its components"-an opening this paper exploits systematically. We argue that, as a general-purpose technology (GPT), AGI simultaneously enhances technology (A), physical capital (K), and labor (L), yielding the generalized production function Y t = A t + ϕ A M t F K t + ϕ K M t , L t + ϕ L M t. The Korinek specification is the special case ϕ A = ϕ K = 0, ϕ L = 1. We derive a multiplicative parameterization, embed it in a Cobb-Douglas framework, develop a knowledge-augmented variant consistent with endogenous growth theory, specify endogenous dynamics for each factor, and perform a six-channel growth accounting decomposition. A Growth Dominance Proposition establishes formally that the generalized model yields weakly higher output and growth than the Korinek benchmark whenever AGI enhances at least one non-labor factor. The paper closes with a research program treating AGI as productive knowledge that functions simultaneously as an input, an output, and a self-reinforcing catalyst of economic growth.

title: The Awareness-Usage Gap in Ancillary Tourism Services: Implications for AI-Driven Service Personalisation -An Exploratory Pilot Study

detail.title: The Awareness-Usage Gap in Ancillary Tourism Services: Implications for AI-Driven Service Personalisation -An Exploratory Pilot Study
detail.abstract: Ancillary services represent an increasingly important revenue stream within the global tourism industry; however, limited research has examined whether tourists explicitly recognise these services despite their widespread usage. This study investigates the relationship between awareness and usage of ancillary tourism services, with particular attention to the potential disconnect between consumer behaviour and conceptual understanding. A quantitative pilot study was conducted using a structured questionnaire administered to 20 international travellers. Descriptive analysis indicates that all respondents reported using at least one ancillary service, including travel insurance, foreign exchange services, and tour-related assistance. However, the majority (60%) were unfamiliar with the term "ancillary services," despite actively engaging with such offerings. The findings suggest the presence of an awareness-usage gap, whereby consumers derive value from services without explicitly recognising them as a distinct category. Positioned as exploratory and hypothesis-generating, the study introduces a novel conceptual perspective on implicit value perception in service consumption. It further offers foundational insights into how behavioural patterns in tourism may inform AIdriven personalisation and recommendation systems.

The full system is demonstrated on Microsoft Corporation (1986-2024) and the U.S. electric vehicle market (2020-2024). The Omega Diagnostic System fills a void in the competitive analysis toolkit: it diagnoses whether market concentration is normal, expanding, or contracting, and what phase of organizational vitality the dominant firm occupies.

detail.abstract: We examine how a workplace health-oriented initiative built around a health-tracking smartwatch affects worker productivity in a field experiment at a large port. Smartwatches that continuously record physiological indicators during working hours were randomly assigned to gantry crane operators. We find that the initiative significantly reduces crane operators’ productivity, lowering weekly throughput by approximately 10%. The decline occurs despite output-based pay and without a detectable treatment effect on perceived organizational monitoring, care, trust, or engagement, providing little evidence that the decline is explained by the distrust-and-crowding-out channel emphasized in the control literature. Instead, exploiting the staged activation of real-time notifications and variation in notification exposure, we find that the decline is most apparent in the period when the notification system is activated and among operators with greater notification exposure, a pattern most consistent with attention diversion. Our results show that a supportive, non-performance-related control system can impose immediate productivity costs through its information and interruption architecture alone, even when it is not perceived as surveillance. The paper offers implications for the design and governance of workplace health and wellness technologies.

title: Strategic Stockpiling under Supply Disruption Risk: Risk-Driven Coordination in Supply Chains

detail.title: Strategic Stockpiling under Supply Disruption Risk: Risk-Driven Coordination in Supply Chains
detail.abstract: Supply disruptions have become increasingly anticipated in global supply chains, prompting firms to build inventory buffers before disruptions materialize. This paper studies how such anticipatory stockpiling affects pricing, inventory decisions, and surplus allocation in a decentralized manufacturer-retailer channel. We develop a two-period model in which a second-period supply disruption occurs with a probability, and firms may carry inventory from the first period to hedge against this risk. We compare three stockpiling structures: retailer-only stockpiling, manufacturer-only stockpiling, and bilateral stockpiling. The analysis shows that disruption risk has heterogeneous effects depending on where inventory is held in the channel. When only the retailer can stockpile, disruption risk may induce the manufacturer to lower the first-period wholesale price, which can benefit the retailer and even improve consumer surplus under certain conditions. When only the manufacturer stockpiles, inventory serves purely as insurance and disruption risk uniformly reduces firm profits and consumer surplus. When both firms can stockpile, disruption risk may intensify inventory competition and shift pricing leverage toward the manufacturer, leading to non-monotonic effects on channel performance. These results reveal a dependence-leverage mechanism through which disruption risk alters vertical pricing incentives. The paper contributes to the literature by integrating supply disruption risk with strategic inventory decisions in decentralized supply chains.

detail.abstract: This paper examines how direct-to-consumer advertising (DTCA) shapes off-label demand for semaglutide. Although semaglutide was initially approved for type 2 diabetes under the brand name Ozempic, its DTCA promoted weight-loss benefits prior to FDA approval of semaglutide for weight management. Using granular prescription and medical claims data from a large sample of commercially-insured individuals, we estimate the effects of DTCA on demand across medical conditions, before and after clinical validation of the weight-management use case. We find that DTCA increases off-label initiation prior to clinical validation, both among individuals without relevant diagnoses and, more strongly, among high BMI individuals, for whom use was later approved. DTCA effects strengthen as clinical evidence accumulates, as does baseline treatment initiation, suggesting the lessening of access frictions. Differential DTCA responses across insurance plans indicate that patients with more generous coverage are better able to convert DTCA-driven interest into initiation, implying greater DTCA-induced exposure to both the potential benefits and risks of early off-label adoption. Overall, our results show that DTCA can accelerate the diffusion of off-label use before formal approval, while providers and insurers shape the distribution of advertising-induced off-label demand.

title: A Reference Architecture for Agentic Data Quality in Microsoft Fabric and Azure

detail.title: A Reference Architecture for Agentic Data Quality in Microsoft Fabric and Azure
detail.abstract: Enterprise data pipelines are increasingly exposed to schema drift, incomplete metadata, statistical anomalies, ambiguous business semantics, and growing operational cost. Conventional rule-based validation remains essential because it is deterministic and auditable, but it becomes expensive to maintain when data sources and business definitions change frequently. Large language models can interpret contextual descriptions and propose mappings or explanations, yet their probabilistic outputs introduce hallucination, privacy, and governance risks. This paper presents a reference architecture for agentic data quality in Microsoft Fabric and Azure that combines deterministic Python and PySpark validation with a bounded Llama-family reasoning layer, structured agent-to-agent communication, and human-in-the-loop review. The design separates structural, statistical, semantic, policy, and governance checks; routes only ambiguous exceptions to an AI model; and records every decision, evidence item, rule version, and reviewer action. Microsoft Fabric provides orchestration, notebooks, OneLake storage, lakehouse tables, semantic models, and reporting, while Azure services provide schema management, event-driven coordination, secrets management, observability, and optional model hosting. The paper does not claim production-scale benchmark results. Instead, it contributes a precise architecture, decision policy, threat model, cost model, and reproducible proof-of-concept protocol using a public retail customer dataset with injected quality faults. The central design principle is controlled autonomy: AI may recommend and explain, but deterministic gates and accountable humans retain authority over high-impact data decisions.

detail.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has rapidly moved from novelty to an everyday tool, and understanding why individuals adopt it has become a central concern for management and information-systems research. The dominant framework for this inquiry, the extended Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT2), is typically estimated using linear, variable-centred methods that report the average effect of each antecedent. A smaller but growing body of work instead applies fuzzy-set and configurational techniques, which treat adoption as arising from combinations of conditions rather than from independent drivers. This review synthesises that body of work. Following PRISMA 2020, we searched five databases and identified seventeen empirical studies that pair UTAUT2 with a fuzzy or configurational method across GenAI and adjacent technologies, appraising each with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Three findings recur. First, performance expectancy and hedonic motivation are the most reliable predictors of adoption intention, whereas effort expectancy and social influence are markedly context-dependent. Second, facilitating conditions and habit relate more strongly to actual use than to intention, suggesting they operate at the stage where decisions become behaviour. Third, the configurational studies show that high adoption is achieved through several distinct and substitutable antecedent combinations rather than a single dominant path. Together, these results indicate that UTAUT2’s explanatory value is conditional on the analytical lens and context, and that fuzzy and configurational methods reveal equifinal, asymmetric adoption patterns that linear models leave hidden. We outline the implications for how GenAI adoption should be modelled

title: World Models: A Survey

detail.title: World Models: A Survey
detail.abstract:
In recent years, a family of machine learning models, the so-called world models, have been attracting growing attention. Particularly, now that large language models (LLMs) have been studied for at least a few years, one may thinker about what comes after large language models. Language models, as their name suggests, typically deal with language-based inputs, e.g., text inputs or other data modalities that can be expressed in some language(s). Such models are mostly trained on enormous amount of text data. As such, LLMs may not be generalized enough for comprehending complex environments, such as the physical world. 
Apparently, world models refer to a concept of more generalized machine learning models that can better comprehend their world (i.e., environment); and thus to abstract, reason and plan more like how intelligent creatures behave in the physical world. As world models are anticipated to be potential candidates for the next frontiers in artificial intelligence, in this article we provide a brief survey of models and neural constructions that are considered or are closely related to world models. We hope this article will be helpful for advancing the state-of-art research in world models.

detail.abstract: Understanding what specific jobs customers are trying to get done has become a longstanding challenge in commercial banking. This paper shows how GenAI embeddings help banks address that problem by shifting the analytical frame from demographic segmentation toward a Jobs to Be Done (JTBD) perspective as understood in the disruptive innovation theory. Drawing on Danske Bank's SpotLight initiative, we demonstrate how embeddings compress complex behavioral data into a form that surfaces product relationships conventional methods tend to miss. detail.abstract: Human oversight of AI systems is resource-intensive, and this challenge becomes acute when National Competent Authorities must verify multiple concurrent AI systems in Article 57 regulatory sandboxes simultaneously. Notions of sandbox governance oversight lack a common operational foundation: verification methodologies are not clearly defined, roles of oversight personnel remain unclear, and approaches to assessing compliance at scale remain unresolved. This paper introduces Smart Simultaneous Governance, a four-layer verification architecture addressing this scalability gap. Layer 1 encodes relevant EU AI Act obligations as executable rules for automated structural checks, Layer 2 selects a risk-proportionate sample with a bounded re-sampling option protecting compliant systems from statistical noise while safeguarding consumer protection, Layer 3 brings independent domain specialists to judge whether sampled outputs cause real harm in practice, and Layer 4 detects demographic bias that individual review cannot see. We argue that AI governance should prioritise quality of oversight over quantity of assessments.

title: Agent-to-Agent Business Ecosystems: Delegated Commercial Agency, Governance, and a Reference Architecture for Autonomous Enterprise Commerce

detail.title: Agent-to-Agent Business Ecosystems: Delegated Commercial Agency, Governance, and a Reference Architecture for Autonomous Enterprise Commerce
detail.abstract: This study examines how interorganizational business ecosystems evolve when organizations transfer bounded commercial decision rights to human or computational organizational representatives that negotiate, commit, and coordinate across firm boundaries while principals retain residual accountability. The manuscript develops a mid-range theory of delegated commercial agency, in which governance capacity produces institutional commercial trust, institutional commercial trust enables the progressive transfer of a separable decision-rights bundle under risk-tiered autonomy, and increasing autonomy reconfigures coordination costs, firm boundaries, value capture, and ecosystem evolution under accountability tensions and competing transaction-cost paths. The theory explains how the joint configuration of governance as a market-enabling capability, unbundled rights redistribution, contingent rather than automatic market expansion, institutional commercial trust, and hybrid agent-centric ecosystem evolution can reshape interorganizational commerce without dissolving firm liability. A reference architecture for Agent-to-Agent (A2A) Business Ecosystems operationalizes the proposed theory. Structured evidence synthesis motivates the underlying mechanisms, while constructs, a nomological network, boundary conditions, and propositions P1-P14 provide a testable theoretical framework. Fully autonomous cross-enterprise commerce at scale is not claimed as a present fact. The study contributes a business theory that conceptualizes autonomous enterprise agents as institutional economic actors operating under delegated commercial authority, extending the discussion of agent-to-agent commerce beyond technical architectures toward governance, institutional trust, and interorganizational business ecosystems.

title: Is Complexity Theory Right that Bigger Is Riskier? Evidence from Information Technology
affiliations: IT University of Copenhagen, IT University of Copenhagen, IT University of Copenhagen, University of Oxford - Said Business School and University of Oxford

detail.title: Is Complexity Theory Right that Bigger Is Riskier? Evidence from Information Technology
detail.abstract: A key thesis in complexity theory is that larger ventures entail higher risk. We test the thesis for information technology (IT) cost and schedule risk. We find that, contrary to common belief, project size is not a reliable predictor of risk. The common assumption that smaller projects have lower risk should be rejected based on our findings. In fact, the smallest IT projects have the largest risk. This finding is significant, because it challenges a central tenet of complexity theory, and it shows project management practitioners that small is not necessarily safe.

detail.abstract: In this note we document the Smart Bond Contract (SBC) pilot conducted by DZ BANK and KfW in March 2026. The pilot implemented the SBC protocol in a legally binding primarymarket transaction for a German crypto security (ISIN DE000SBC0DZ4) and demonstrated a complete deterministic lifecycle for a tokenized security on a public blockchain. The workflow covered on-chain publication of funding levels and digital transaction documentation, on-chain ISIN assignment, automated registration in a crypto securities register, token minting, decentralized Delivery-versus-Payment issuance, and final redemption settlement. Each step was executed by interconnected smart contracts on Polygon PoS without a central operator holding state or controlling the process. The transaction connected six market functions in direct peer-to-peer interaction: DZ BANK as issuer, KfW as investor, WM Datenservice as ISIN provider, Cashlink as crypto securities registrar, Deutsche Bundesbank as provider of the Trigger Solution for final cash settlement in central bank money in T2, and an NTT DATA-hosted decryption oracle. The pilot shows that the SBC concept can operate as an infrastructure-agnostic protocol rather than as a platform-specific workflow. By proving deterministic execution, modular process design, and intraday finality across issuance and redemption, the pilot provides practical evidence that tokenized securities lifecycle processes can be implemented transparently and without platform dependency.

detail.abstract: The Supreme Court of the United States confronts a crisis of legitimacy not because it decides wrongly, but because it decides opaquely. When constitutional interpretation shifts abruptly across decades—from Plessy to Brown, from Cruikshank to Heller—the public receives no empirical account of why the law changed beyond the assertion of judicial authority. This paper diagnoses this condition as epistemic capture: the gradual institutional loss of capacity to detect interpretive drift. Drawing on the Calibration Thesis, Faithful Intelligence governance principles, and design science methodology, the paper proposes a Constitutional Integrity Monitor (CIM)—an epistemic governance architecture that audits interpretive reasoning through statistical variance detection. The CIM does not decide cases; it measures the distance between proposed interpretations and the constitutional record through Analogical Gravity Mapping. Addressing the central vulnerability of algorithmic governance, the CIM integrates a formal contestation mechanism including a Weighting Review Board, an appeal protocol, and a minority dissent archive. The paper demonstrates through historical case analysis how the CIM would document interpretive evolution in landmark cases without endorsing any particular constitutional theory, and concludes that constitutional fidelity is served not by judicial mystique but by calibration transparency: the continuous alignment of interpretive authority with constitutional verification realities.

title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption and Financial Performance: Empirical Evidence from Emerging Markets with a Focus on Bangladesh

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption and Financial Performance: Empirical Evidence from Emerging Markets with a Focus on Bangladesh
detail.abstract: This study examines the relationship between Artificial Intelligence (AI) adoption and firm-level financial performance in emerging markets, with a particular focus on Bangladesh. Using a balanced panel of 60 firms listed on the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) over 2018-2024, complemented by macroeconomic indicators from the World Bank, the paper applies fixed-and random-effects panel regression alongside ensemble machine-learning models (Random Forest and Gradient Boosting) to evaluate the impact of AI adoption on Return on Assets (ROA), Return on Equity (ROE), and net profit margin. The findings indicate that AI adoption significantly enhances firm performance by improving operational efficiency, reducing costs, and enabling data-driven decisionmaking. Each one-standard-deviation increase in the AI Adoption Index is associated with a 1.46-percentage-point increase in ROA after controlling for firm size, leverage, and industry effects. Results are robust across model specifications and validated by machine-learning predictions achieving 82-88% out-of-sample accuracy. The paper contributes to the literature by integrating traditional financial econometrics with modern AI-driven analytics in the context of a developing economy and offers actionable policy implications for accelerating digital transformation.

detail.abstract: Women play a central role in Nigeria's informal and cross-border trade sector, contributing significantly to household welfare, local economies, and regional commerce. Despite accounting for the majority of informal cross-border traders, their contributions remain largely invisible in formal economic statistics and trade policymaking. This paper examines the participation of women in Nigeria's informal and cross-border trade, focusing on their socioeconomic characteristics, economic contributions, and the challenges they face, including financial exclusion, inadequate infrastructure, harassment at border crossings, and the burden of unpaid care work. The paper further analyzes the impact of regional trade frameworks, particularly the ECOWAS Protocols and the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), on women traders and assesses the extent to which these initiatives address gender-specific barriers. It argues that trade liberalization alone is insufficient to improve women's economic opportunities without complementary policies that promote financial inclusion, security, infrastructure development, social protection, and gender-responsive governance. By highlighting both the vulnerabilities and resilience of women traders, the paper underscores the need for inclusive trade policies that recognize and support their contributions to sustainable economic development and regional integration in Nigeria and West Africa.

title: Are Union Co-op Labor Negotiations a Win-Win and for Whom?

detail.title: Are Union Co-op Labor Negotiations a Win-Win and for Whom?

declarations.ethicsApproval: University of Louisville IRB approval 23.0831 - "Are union co-op labor negotiations a win-win and for whom?"

detail.abstract: Are union co-op labor negotiations in the United States more similar to the interest-based win-win negotiation framework popularized by Getting to Yes than traditional labor negotiations? If they are, do co-op labor negotiations and resultant collective bargaining agreements (CBAs) address some of the grand challenges of this historical time? This article explores how union negotiations in worker-owned co-ops compare to more traditional labor negotiations. Interviews with participants in union co-op collective bargaining and a review of several union co-op collective bargaining agreements suggest that many union co-op labor negotiations are more similar to interest-based negotiations than traditional labor negotiations. Those involved described these negotiations as more transparent, involving greater exchange of information, and oriented more toward cooperative problem-solving than traditional negotiations. Some agreements reference interest-based negotiations and others cooperative principles. The structure of the union cooperative may facilitate interest-based negotiations because of the greater sharing of information, including financial information, than in traditional negotiations and the orientation toward cooperative principles. Resultant advantages may include: 1) higher satisfaction from participants with the process and outcomes, and 2) workers gaining financial literacy and practicing problem-solving skills transferable to other settings.  The second part of this paper  provides background about the operations of more traditional labor negotiations in the United States and about the limited instances and business frameworks where collective bargaining and employee ownership intersect. The third part of the paper briefly describes union co-op labor negotiations to familiarize the reader with negotiation in this sector. In the fourth part, the paper expounds the theoretical framework from which the union co-op labor negotiations will be explored – the dispute resolution theories of distributive versus interest-based bargaining. In the final part, the paper analyzes several union co-op negotiations and resultant CBAs and addresses the questions posed at the outset of the research and this paper.

title: A Quantitative Analysis of Security Breaches in the Digital Financial Sector and Organizational Commitment to People’s Security

detail.title: A Quantitative Analysis of Security Breaches in the Digital Financial Sector and Organizational Commitment to People’s Security
detail.abstract: This thesis explores how dedicating resources to people-focused security measures influences the likelihood of data breaches in the global financial industry. Although previous studies have connected broad cybersecurity practices to breach rates, few have zoomed in on investments in human capital as a riskmitigation strategy for banks, financial technology firms (fintechs), and other financial institutions. To fill this gap, we conducted a cross‐sectional quantitative survey of 50 security practitioners engaged via LinkedIn that reached seasoned security professionals across multiple countries. We then categorized responses on employee training, awareness campaigns, and dedicated security budgets. This thesis observes patterns linking these investments to actual security breach events. This thesis hypothesizes that firms allocating more to workforce security will report fewer incidents, though we expect factors like company size and regional regulation to modulate this effect. Our findings aim both to enrich academic discussions around the “people” dimension of cybersecurity and to offer practical guidance on crafting cost-effective, human-centered defenses. Future work might compare these results across other sectors or track changes over time to build on our initial insights.

title: The Dual Experiential Spiral: A Framework for Faculty-Student AI Literacy Co-Development in Higher Education
affiliations: and University of Pittsburgh - Department of Economics

detail.title: The Dual Experiential Spiral: A Framework for Faculty-Student AI Literacy Co-Development in Higher Education
detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Dual Experiential Spiral (DES), a theoretical framework for understanding AI literacy in higher education as a co-developmental faculty-student process rather than two parallel institutional problems. Faculty AI literacy and student AI literacy are typically addressed through separate professional development tracks and student-facing programs. We argue this siloed approach is theoretically incomplete because the two are coupled processes whose interaction may substantially shape the development of both. Drawing on Kolb's (1984) experiential learning spiral, Vygotsky's (1978) Zone of Proximal Development, and Davis's (1989) Technology Acceptance Model, DES proposes that two interdependent learning spiralsone for faculty and one for students-become coupled through structured AI engagement in the shared classroom. We advance three testable propositions: (1) both populations develop AI literacy through upward experiential spirals; (2) structured classroom AI engagement couples these spirals through bidirectional feedback; and (3) coupling requires three enabling conditions: structured contact, bidirectional feedback flow, and mutual psychological safety. We also specify boundary conditions under which coupling may fail, including institutional reward structures that reinforce one-way delivery, top-down mandates without participation, and student compliance without authentic engagement. Implications are drawn for course design, institutional investment, educational equity, and research methodology in higher education systems globally.

detail.title: Capital Cliffs and EU Securitisation Regulations
detail.abstract: This report assesses cliff effects in European securitisation capital rules. Capital cliffs create distortions and exacerbate instability in financial stress periods. Regulators work to remove such cliffs when memories of financial crises are fresh. But cliffs may creep back as the authorities fine-tune earlier decisions and recollection of stress conditions fades. Right now, European regulators, aware of the region's investment needs, are considering adjustments aimed at reviving the securitisation market. This study argues that those designing the new rules should take steps to identify and remove cliff effects from the framework.

title: Guarantee Companies & Development Finance: Products, Business Models & Constraints
