detail.title: On the Trade-Off Between Calibration and Discrimination in Credit Risk Modeling: A Financial Value Perspective
detail.abstract: Translating statistical modeling into tangible business value remains a central challenge for quantitative risk management in financial institutions. This paper bridges the gap between statistical theory and banking practice by evaluating the fundamental trade-off between predictive model calibration and discriminatory power in binary credit cycle prediction problems. We analyze core performance metrics-specifically the calibration curve, the Brier Score and its Murphy decomposition (uncertainty, reliability, and resolution), the Gini coefficient, and the Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) statistic-to demonstrate how their mathematical properties dictate institutional decision-making under modern regulatory frameworks like IFRS-9. Beyond pure statistical verification, we formalize the operational and financial implications of these metrics. We discuss how miscalibration compromises capital reservation and expected loss frameworks, while insufficient discriminative power triggers destructive adverse selection dynamics in competitive lending markets. Finally, the impacts of these dynamics on expected loss performance are exposed.

title: Are Securities Transaction Taxes Capitalized? Evidence from A-H Twins around China's Stamp-Duty Shocks

detail.title: Are Securities Transaction Taxes Capitalized? Evidence from A-H Twins around China's Stamp-Duty Shocks
detail.abstract: Whether a securities transaction tax is capitalized into prices is central to the financial-transaction-tax debate, but is hard to identify because a market-wide tax change moves the whole market at once. We solve the no-control-group problem using Chinese firms cross-listed in Shanghai/Shenzhen (A-shares) and Hong Kong (H-shares): China's stamp duty applies only to onshore A-share trading, so the H-share leg of the same firm is an untreated within-firm control. We study two clean, oppositely-signed natural experiments—the 2007 stamp-duty hike (0.1%→0.3%) and the 2023 cut (0.1%→0.05%)—and exclude the 2008 episodes, which fall in the depth of the global financial crisis. The A-H premium moves in the predicted direction in both cases: it falls by about 5.4% on the 2007 hike (in the 2nd percentile of the placebo distribution, p ≈ 0.02) and rises by about 0.9% on the 2023 cut (cross-firm t ≈ 6, though only the 91st placebo percentile, p ≈ 0.09). The 2023 response is transitory and unrelated to firm-level turnover, and the 2008 crisis cut moved the premium the "wrong" way. The evidence indicates that an A-share-specific tax change is rapidly priced into the segmented-market wedge on announcement, but as a transient, sentiment-like response rather than the permanent, turnover-scaled adjustment that textbook capitalization implies—and that its strength depends on the prevailing confidence regime. Securities transaction taxes are thus "priced" but not cleanly "capitalized."

detail.title: A Hierarchical Plug-in Framework for Dual-Role Post-hoc Explanation
detail.abstract: Post-hoc visual explanation methods often summarize a model decision with a single attribution or saliency signal, although the evidence sufficient to sustain a prediction and the evidence on which the predictor critically relies may differ. This paper proposes a hierarchical plug-in framework for dual-role post-hoc explanation of frozen visual predictors. An Illumination Sensitivity Generator first learns a sample-adaptive predictive-sensitivity path. An Essentiality Explainer then identifies compact support-oriented evidence that preserves the target prediction under this learned reference, while a Vulnerability Explainer inherits the essentiality context and generates localized perturbations to reveal decision-critical evidence. The predictor remains unchanged, making the framework applicable to heterogeneous visual backbones. Experiments on CUB-200-2011 and a brain tumor magnetic resonance imaging dataset with ViT- and ResNet-based frozen predictors show differentiated localization and preservation behavior across the two branches, substantial vulnerability suppression under compact perturbation, complementary explanation roles, and moderate explanation cost. Ablation studies further examine the contributions of the learned sensitivity path and inherited explanatory context. These results indicate that separating explanatory roles can provide a more specific post-hoc account of visual pattern recognition models.

detail.abstract: War is usually understood through destruction, mobilization, or technological invention. This paper proposes a fourth analytical frame: war as a reorganization machine. It argues that war reorganizes systems not because violence automatically creates order, but because extreme pressure can make inherited arrangements too costly to preserve. When repeated tactical failure raises pressure on an existing function-carrier relation beyond an organization's preservation capacity, actors are more likely to recombine available resources into new mediating tools. These tools, in turn, test whether organizations can absorb failure, revise routines, alter procurement priorities, and sustain relevance under adversarial adaptation. The paper develops a threshold mechanism linking war pressure, tactical blockage, resource recombination, adaptive organization, procurement and industrial revaluation, infrastructural spillover, and possible social sedimentation. The cases of tanks and drones are used as structural illustrations rather than full historical narratives: both reveal how blocked functions can be preserved through new configurations of available resources. The paper then extends the mechanism beyond tools, showing how adaptive demands may pull civilian and commercial infrastructures into security relevance and how some wartime arrangements may sediment into peacetime routines, institutions, or governance categories. The framework is not deterministic and does not claim that all wars generate deep transformation. It specifies observable propositions, measurable proxy indicators, scope conditions, negative cases, and falsification paths. Its contribution is connective: it links battlefield pressure to organizational, industrial, infrastructural, and social change without reducing the process to technological determinism, state command, or war functionalism. Reorganization is not justification. The paper offers a connective mid-range theory of systemic transformation under extreme pressure.

detail.abstract:
Abstract and Research Contribution

The international order that shaped the post-war economy is undergoing a structural transformation. Assumptions that long underpinned global finance, including expanding economic integration, politically neutral financial infrastructure, stable legal frameworks, and the predictable movement of capital - are increasingly challenged by geopolitical fragmentation, strategic competition, technological disruption, and the growing convergence of economics and national security. This paper argues that these developments should not be understood as a sequence of temporary crises, but as evidence of a transition toward a fundamentally different institutional environment.

Against this background, the paper proposes a shift in analytical perspective. Rather than treating capital allocation, financial innovation, or technological advancement as the primary determinants of long-term success, it identifies institutional architecture as the decisive strategic variable of the twenty-first century. The central argument is that durable prosperity depends less on the accumulation of assets than on the ability of institutions to preserve trust, legal certainty, continuity, and settlement capacity under conditions of systemic uncertainty.

Drawing upon institutional economics, monetary theory, governance, complexity science, geopolitical strategy, and economic history, the study develops a conceptual framework for understanding the ongoing transition from an era characterized primarily by financial competition to one increasingly defined by institutional competition. It examines how resilience is replacing efficiency as a strategic priority, why continuity has become a competitive capability rather than an administrative objective, and how trust is evolving from an implicit characteristic of the international system into an asset that individual institutions must deliberately design, protect, and sustain.

The study concludes that the defining challenge of the coming decades is not simply adapting existing financial structures to new circumstances but designing institutions capable of maintaining legitimacy and confidence across jurisdictions, generations, technological disruption, and geopolitical change. In this emerging environment, enduring competitive advantage will belong not to those who control the greatest quantity of capital, but to those who build institutional architectures worthy of tomorrow's trust.

detail.title: Adaptive Information Bottleneck-Aware Multi-instance Learning for Whole Slide Image Classification
detail.abstract: In pathological image analysis, whole slide image (WSI) provides critical support for cancer diagnosis. Since WSI have gigapixel resolution and lack region-level annotations, directly conducting end-to-end learning will consume computational resources. Multi-instance learning (MIL) has become a processing paradigm for WSI because it can perform inference with only the WSI-level label. However, most current MIL methods neglect semantic interactions between instances and struggle to model discriminative instance structures across all bags. Thereby undermining the information bottleneck (IB) principle, which seeks to maximize input-output correlation. We propose an adaptive information bottleneck-aware multi-instance learning (AIBMIL), which with two components. Firstly, the primary-auxiliary cluster reconstruction and fusion lies in partitioning the data in each bag into discriminative primary cluster bag (PCB) and auxiliary cluster bag (ACB). Guiding the aggregation of instance features toward PCB, thereby addressing redundancy and insufficient discriminative power in intra-bag features and effectively reducing the intra-bag IB value.Secondly, the global contrast and diversity regularization is used to generate more stable and distinguishable bag-level representations across bags at the global-bag level. To supplement by diversity regularization to mitigate feature collapse, a momentum prototype and triple constraints are used to bring the primary cluster closer and push the auxiliary cluster farther away. Experiments show the efficiency of AIBMIL on WSI datasets. When applied as an independent method, it achieves the best performance across WSI datasets, and as a plug-in, it yields improvements in 30 out of 36 experiments while preserving the original hyperparameter settings.​

detail.abstract: This paper traces the intellectual evolution of environmental and ecological economics from early critiques of technocratic development to contemporary climate-change debates. It situates Herman Daly's steady-state framework within competing traditions-market environmentalism, population-limits discourse, environmental-conflict theory, biodiversity governance, green political thought, and ecological health-and argues that these traditions converge on a single diagnostic: conventional economics systematically undervalues the ecological foundations of production. The analysis integrates foundational contributions on exhaustible and renewable resource economics, the blue economy, green economy transitions, and the political economy of global inequality to deepen the theoretical foundations. To operationalise this diagnosis, the paper develops a generalised land theory of value in which land is a multidimensional asset defined by ecological integrity, biodiversity, cultural significance, and scale. A formal ecological-dynamics model is derived, and an empirical panel-data specification links these ecological variables to agricultural productivity across countries. Illustrative regression results, robustness checks, and replication code are provided. The findings reinforce the case for integrating ecological constraints into economic theory, national accounts, and environmental policy. All empirical results are illustrative, generated from a stylised data structure to demonstrate the specification; estimation on the full crosscountry panel is ongoing.

detail.abstract: This paper analyzes the interaction of unlimited labor supply, transformative artificial intelligence (AI), and endogenous growth dynamics. We synthesize Romer (1986, 1990, 1993), Lucas (1988, 1993), and Aghion and Howitt (1992, 1998), together with the broader literature on creative destruction, to examine conditions under which growth persists as well as scenarios of stagnation or decline. The analysis highlights policy implications for both developing and industrialized economies, with particular attention to low-income countries. An illustrative case study using synthetic data—calibrated to stylized facts of Ghana, a representative lower-middle income, labor-abundant economy in sub-Saharan Africa—demonstrates how such an economy might navigate the transition to an AI-augmented growth path under three distinct policy regimes. A discussion of the substitution-versus-complementarity dimension of AI adoption shows that the mode of AI deployment, not merely its extent, is decisive for labor-market and distributional outcomes.

detail.abstract: The real order of Argentina's relationship with Lionel Messi runs from discard to derision and from derision to appropriation, and the prevailing narrative inverts it into a devotion that was always there. The local footballing system detected the talent without difficulty and did not sustain the growth-hormone treatment the boy's body required, so it let him go at twelve to a club that could afford it; over the following decade a dominant current of the fans and the press called him a "pecho frío"-a cold-chested player, in an explicitly gendered insult-and suspected he preferred Spain, where he had been formed, to his own country, scorn that culminated in his resignation from the national team in 2016; only with the titles of 2021, 2022 and 2026 did the same machinery that had discarded and humiliated him consecrate him as the greatest Argentine in history. The article holds, against the sentimental reading, that the derision targeted a foreignness the Argentine system itself manufactured by failing to retain him, and that the present devotion is materially produced memory whose central operation is not to remember but to erase the first two phases. All references were verified using the RICON-3 protocol: documentary existence, bibliographic coherence and semantic relevance.

title: The Observation Portfolio: Why Budget Cannot Move the Blind Spot

detail.title: The Observation Portfolio: Why Budget Cannot Move the Blind Spot
detail.abstract: A single monitor who splits a nite attention budget across tasks does not, in general, cover the tasks where failure is costliest. We show that across such an observation portfolio, coverage is sorted by the composition of responsibility the reach-contingent blame dierential ∆ that xes how much of a residual failure is attributed to the monitor and not by the budget. The marginal blame incurred by observing is largest exactly where the stakes are highest, so the highest-stakes task is the most toxic to look at; under a binding budget the monitor abandons it, and no budget recovers it, because a trapped task is incentive-constrained, not budgetconstrained. Only redesigning the responsibility regime lowering ∆, or raising the production response g = Q ′ (0) does. The result holds on one side of a regime boundary whose master variable is g, unifying it with the productive-observation cascade of the companion programme; the budget-rationing blind spot that arises on the other side sorts by the opposite attribute, so the two are empirically separable. Recurring control deciencies on high-stakes tasks then read as a portfolio blind spot, not a resourcing failure.

detail.abstract: Electric vehicles are widely promoted as a way to reduce carbon emissions, but do they always do so? The answer depends on the electricity used for charging, whose carbon intensity varies substantially across U.S. states and over time. While many studies examine EV emissions, relatively few estimate the net CO2 effect at the state level. Using a bottom-up plant-level dispatch model covering all 50 states and the District of Columbia, this study compares emissions from EV charging with the gasoline emissions avoided under three charging schedules, unmanaged, partially managed, and fully managed, and across fleet sizes. Results show that the generation mix serving incremental electricity demand and fleet size largely determine net emissions, whereas charging schedules have a comparatively smaller effect because shifting charging often reallocates demand among generators with similar marginal emissions. Overall, EV adoption reduces national CO2 emissions by approximately 90 to 100 million tonnes annually, although benefits vary substantially across states, with 37 of 51 seeing a net reduction, though some only marginally, while in 14 coal-reliant states electric vehicles raise emissions rather than lower them. The findings suggest that the generation mix on the margin and the size of the EV fleet matter more for emissions than the timing of charging. Policymakers should act on three fronts at once. They should push the power plants that supply new demand to be cleaner, speed up the shift to electric vehicles, and, where a cleaner plant is available at another time of day, encourage charging at that time. Because the plant that responds to new demand differs from state to state, these actions should be tailored to each state rather than set by a single national rule. Acting on all three together delivers far larger emissions cuts than any one alone.

detail.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of Sudan's ongoing multidimensional crisis, examining the interplay between armed conflict, economic disintegration, and demographic transformation through the lenses of socioeconomic and demographic theory. Since April 2023, Sudan has experienced what the United Nations characterizes as the world's largest displacement crisis, with over 14 million people forcibly displaced and more than 33 million in need of humanitarian assistance. The conflict between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) has not only devastated the nation's physical infrastructure but has also precipitated an economic collapse characterized by currency depreciation exceeding 80%, hyperinflation reaching 145%, and the fragmentation of state institutions. This paper argues that Sudan's crisis cannot be understood through any single analytical lens; rather, it represents a complex intersection of resource scarcity, institutional failure, external intervention, and deliberate demographic engineering. Drawing on resource conflict theory, political economy analysis, and demographic transition theory, the paper examines five interconnected dimensions: (1) the military fragmentation and proliferation of armed groups; (2) the political economy of fuel imports and the Aramco proposal; (3) the de facto territorial partition and emergence of parallel governance structures; (4) demographic engineering and population displacement; and (5) the erosion of state sovereignty and national security. The paper further develops four plausible future scenarios and proposes a comprehensive framework for sustainable resolution. The paper concludes that sustainable resolution requires integrated approaches addressing security sector reform, economic restructuring, and demographic reconciliation, while warning that continued inaction risks permanent state fragmentation.

detail.abstract: This paper advances the thesis that the removal of three zeros from the Sudanese pound, a policy of currency redenomination, constitutes an essential, though not sufficient, condition for restoring monetary stability and facilitating economic recovery in post-conflict Sudan. Drawing on the theoretical frameworks of monetary supply and demand, the fiscal theory of the price level, and the quantity theory of money, the analysis demonstrates that Sudan's monetary aggregates have expanded exponentially. At the same time, real output has collapsed, producing a hyperinflationary dynamic that has rendered the national currency functionally useless as a store of value and unit of account. The paper presents empirical evidence showing that Broad Money M2 grew from 7.6 trillion to over 26.7 trillion Sudanese pounds between December 2023 and January 2026, while real GDP contracted by an estimated 29.4% in 2023 and by a further 14% in 2024, among the steepest economic contractions in recent history. Through comparative analysis of successful redenomination experiences in Turkey, Brazil, Argentina, and post-WWII Germany, the paper establishes that currency restructuring, when accompanied by complementary fiscal and institutional reforms, can restore confidence, simplify transactions, reduce transaction costs, and create the psychological and operational conditions for economic recovery. The paper further argues that Sudan's exceptionally low Corruption Perceptions Index score of 14/100 and the weaponization of monetary policy for war financing necessitate that redenomination be implemented alongside comprehensive institutional reforms addressing deficit monetization, central bank independence, and accountability mechanisms. The paper concludes that while removing three zeros from the Sudanese pound is not a panacea, it is an indispensable component of a broader monetary and fiscal reform package essential for Sudan's economic reconstruction.

detail.abstract: I examine the legal, political, and institutional transformations that have affected higher education governance in Sudan over a period of five decades (1970-2021). Drawing primarily on Issam AW Mohamed's comprehensive manuscript, Thoughts and Proposals on the Organization of Higher Education in Sudan (Issam AW Mohamed, 2012). My analysis traces four major legislative instruments: the 1975 Higher Education Organization Law, the 1985 law issued after the April Revolution, the 1990 decree under the National Islamic Front (Salvation regime), and the 2021 Higher Education and Scientific Research Organization Law. Drawing on of university autonomy that distinguishes organizational, financial, staffing, and academic dimensions (European University Association, 2017), I show how successive regimes slowly took control away from campuses, made hiring political, limited what teachers could say, forced curricula to follow ideology, and turned universities from places that ask questions into tools for rewarding supporters. I built this analysis on documents such as the referenced internal reports (Ahmed & Mihaisi, 1982. El Tigani et al., 1996; UNESCO, 1993) that provide firsthand testimonies from within the system. To ground the legal analysis, I present illustrative socioeconomic and demographic estimates, including gross enrollment rates, public expenditure per student, student-faculty ratios, youth unemployment, and graduate unemployment, that show how centralized governance affected the daily lives of real people. The figures suggest that while the number of public universities has grown from 4 in 1970 to over 35 in 2025, public expenditure per student has declined by more than 40% since 2000, the student-faculty ratio has reached 65:1, and graduate unemployment exceeds 48%. These trends go hand in hand with the erosion of the capacity of universities to govern themselves independently. For a student, that means sitting on the floor in a crowded hall. For a teacher, it means grading hundreds of papers alone at night. In practice, reform proposals, which are presented in systematic detail, include: replacing the Ministry of Higher Education with an independent National Coordination Council attached to the Prime Minister's office. re-establishing a tripartite system of universities (4-year bachelor's), higher institutes (2-3 year diplomas), and community colleges (2-year certificates). decentralizing funding through direct university-Ministry of Finance budget negotiations. abolishing all political, regional, and dollar-based admission quotas. restoring democratic elections for university leadership. and removing ideological designations from specific institutions (e.g., Omdurman Islamic University, Africa University). The paper argues that without the immediate suspension of the 2021 law and a fundamental reversal of centralized governance backed by political will from the transitional government and international partners Sudanese higher education cannot recover its former regional standing, address the youth employment crisis, or contribute to democratic development.

detail.abstract: Building on the empirical findings and mathematical theorems of the previous two papers, this paper completes the theoretical derivation of the gauge group structure of the Standard Model from the Factor Hierarchy Law. The meta-regime factor (color charge) satisfies three conditions: dividing particles into mutually exclusive regimes, having irreducible interaction effects, and modulating all executive factors — these conditions mathematically define exactly the generators of a discrete symmetry group. Given that color charge is a meta-regime factor with three mutually exclusive regime states (the latter being a known fact of the Standard Model), SU(3) is the unique gauge group satisfying the conditions. The orthogonal independence of color charge and flavor quantum numbers (confirmed in Paper 15) implies that the two meta-regime factors act independently on distinct internal spaces, so their gauge groups must form a direct product. The SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1) structure of the Standard Model is not an arbitrarily written assumption but an inevitable algebraic consequence of this rule. The topological constraint of the transition zone width, together with the experimental exclusion of a fourth generation of quarks by the LHC, jointly points to the number of heavy quarks being limited to four. The four regime centers (strange, charm, bottom, top) fill the mass range from approximately 1.5 GeV to approximately 172.6 GeV. The spacing from bottom to top (162.4 GeV) already far exceeds those from strange to charm (0.8 GeV) and from charm to bottom (7.17 GeV); the spacing of a fifth regime center would be even larger, and its transition zone width would cover a vast region above the electroweak unification scale. The two theorems and one proposition proved in this paper — the Gauge Group Structure Theorem (Theorem 4), the Direct Product Theorem (Theorem 5), and the Three-Generation Proposition (Proposition 6) — together constitute the demonstration of the inevitable emergence of the gauge group structure from regime boundaries. Gauge field theory is not the most fundamental theoretical framework — it is the expression of regime boundaries in the language of group theory. The Factor Hierarchy Law is an organizing principle deeper than gauge field theory. As the third paper of the five-paper series, this paper completes this crucial theoretical leap, providing the core theoretical pillar for the conceptual reinterpretations and system legislation of the subsequent two papers.

First layer: An exhaustive scan of 11 activation operators reveals that the operators automatically stratify by their optimal breakpoints into two groups: the charm region (~2.29 GeV) and the bottom region (~9.46–10.02 GeV). No operator chooses the intermediate zone — activation operators are regime selectors, not signal amplifiers.

Second layer: The W×M² activation operator amplifies the Chow F statistic from 31.98 to 81,540 — an amplification factor of 2569×. This is the statistical manifestation of the pole structure of the Breit-Wigner amplitude. Its breakpoint, 10.0234 GeV, deviates from the PDG standard value of the Υ(2S) bottomonium state (10.023 GeV) by only 0.0004 GeV.
Third layer: The charm-region breakpoint of 2.2865 GeV deviates from the PDG standard value of the Λc⁺ charmed baryon (2.28646 GeV) by 0.00004 GeV. The bottom-region W×M breakpoint of 9.4603 GeV deviates from the Υ(1S) standard value (9.46030 GeV) by 0.0001 GeV. Completely unaware of the physical meaning of these particles, the algorithm automatically locks their positions with professional phenomenological fitting precision, revealing a hitherto unrecognized methodological function of known particles: they are the "nails" of regime switches in the data.

Six structural break tools — Chow, Bai-Perron, SupF, CUSUM, MOSUM, and ICSS — provide cross-verification. Blank controls (F-value only 24% of the true breakpoint), multi-interval blank scans, permutation tests (p = 0.002), bootstrap (median 2.11 GeV), conditional independence tests, and reverse proxy tests jointly rule out statistical artifacts and alternative explanations. Mass is confirmed as a dual-identity factor — the first empirical confirmation of the Factor Hierarchy Law's classification framework in particle physics.

As the first of a five-paper series, this paper establishes the existence of two regime-switching centers (charm and bottom), providing the indispensable empirical foundation for the derivation of regime boundary theorems and the inevitable emergence of gauge group structures in subsequent papers.

detail.abstract:
India’s “GST 2.0” reform of 22 September 2025 collapsed a four-rate schedule into two principal slabs; the government’s stated rationale was that fewer rates would produce fewer classification disputes. This paper tests that claim against an updated census of 3,009 published Authority for Advance Ruling (AAR) decisions, coded by statutory issue under Section 97(2) of the CGST Act, 2017. The pre-reform window comprises every ruling up to and including December 2025; the post-reform window comprises January 2026 onward, the earliest interval in which decisions can be attributed with reasonable confidence to post-reform applications. Pre- and post-reform classification shares are compared using two-proportion z-tests, and a linear trend test on the pre-reform annual series determines whether any post-reform change constitutes a genuine structural break.

The findings are consistent across both the primary and strict classification coding rules. Instead of declining, the share of classification disputes rose significantly after the reform — from 69.3 per cent in the pre-reform period to 91.7 per cent in the post-reform window (z = +4.71, p < 0.001). The pre-reform trend is statistically flat (slope: +0.46 percentage points per year; p = 0.580), confirming that the post-reform jump is a discontinuity rather than the continuation of prior drift. The point estimate of strict-classification monthly volume also rose (8.6 to 15.4 rulings per month), but with only five post-reform months this absolute-count difference is not statistically significant (Welch t = 2.18, p = 0.062); the headline finding therefore rests on the share-based tests. Companion enforcement signals like DGGI evasion detections at a record ₹2.23 lakh crore in FY25, a GST Appellate Tribunal backlog exceeding four lakh appeals from its opening day, and CBIC’s own acknowledgment of proliferating High Court writ petitions, all corroborating that aggregate dispute volumes are rising, not falling.

Taken together, the evidence rejects the government’s dispute-reduction claim. GST 2.0 did not reduce classification disputes; on the recorded evidence, the post-reform period exhibits a significantly higher share and absolute volume of classification litigation.

title: Self-Consistency Rupture in Stellar Atmosphere Models: The Second Astronomical Empirical Case for the Factor Hierarchy Law——Evidence from Internal Cross-Validation Based on the Four-Test Method

detail.title: Self-Consistency Rupture in Stellar Atmosphere Models: The Second Astronomical Empirical Case for the Factor Hierarchy Law——Evidence from Internal Cross-Validation Based on the Four-Test Method
detail.abstract: Core Conclusions: (1) Stellar atmosphere models exhibit a structural self-consistency rupture on either side of the critical points of 4762 K and log g = 4.64. (2) The model-derived density and the independent asteroseismic density display systematic deviations across these critical thresholds that cannot be explained by random error. (3) The model's underlying assumptions—one-dimensional static atmospheres, local thermodynamic equilibrium, and mixing-length theory—systematically fail for cool stars and evolved stars. This study applies the Principle of Testability and the Four-Test Method proposed by Tang (2026g), augmented by the 5W2H and PDCA completeness frameworks, to perform an internal cross-validation on the stellar host data of 18,116 transiting planets from the NASA Exoplanet Archive. A model-dependent density is constructed from the model output values of stellar radius and mass, and a logarithmic residual analysis is performed against the independent asteroseismic density. Exhaustive testing automatically selected st_logg + st_met as the optimal combination from the candidate executing factors (adjusted R² = 0.019). Interaction effect testing revealed that stellar spectral type systematically modulates the exposure coefficients of st_logg and st_met on the density residual (spec_Unknown × st_logg: p = 3.62×10⁻²⁰). Chow tests confirmed that the density residual equation undergoes a structural break at the temperature threshold of 4762 K (F = 6.66, p = 0.00017), the surface gravity threshold of log g = 4.64 (F = 10.40, p = 7.91×10⁻⁷), and between metallicity groups (metal-poor vs. Solar: F = 14.50, p = 2.00×10⁻⁹). The matched-sample test for the surface gravity Chow test is robust (91% of draws significant), and the matched-sample test for the temperature Chow test confirms the signal is genuine (64% of draws significant, median F = 3.33). Permutation tests (empirical p = 0.002) and quantile regressions (0.75 quantile: inter_temp_st_met p = 3.35×10⁻¹³) provide comprehensive support for the conclusions. The findings of this paper are fully isomorphic with the regime coupling discovered by Tang (2026h) in transit depth measurements—the two converge at the same critical points. The combined evidence indicates that the paradigm defect in exoplanet radius measurement originates from the systematic failure of the underlying assumptions of stellar atmosphere models for cool stars and evolved stars. Taken together with the discoveries of Tang (2026g) across five major financial markets, and the independent verifications by Tang (2026h) and this paper in astronomy, Factor Hierarchy Theory has accumulated sufficient cross-disciplinary and cross-dimensional evidence. This paper recommends performing a Chow test to confirm model self-consistency before applying stellar atmosphere models across regimes.

detail.abstract: Industrial park development has become a key policy instrument for promoting industrialization and economic transformation in developing countries. However, empirical evidence on its effects on labor market and domestic investment outcomes remains limited in Ethiopia. This study examines the impact of industrial park development on labor market and domestic investment outcomes in Ethiopia using panel data from treated and control zones. A Difference-inDifferences (DID) estimation approach is employed to identify the causal effects of industrial park development while controlling for time-invariant unobserved heterogeneity and common time trends. The analysis focuses on labor market outcomes, measured by employee wages, commissions and professional allowances, and employment generation, as well as domestic investment outcomes, measured by the number of domestic investors, paid-up capital, and working capital. The findings reveal that industrial park development has significantly improved labor market outcomes by increasing employee wages, compensation, and employment opportunities, including female employment. In contrast, the analysis finds no statistically significant effect on domestic investment outcomes, suggesting that the expected spillover effects on domestic private investment have not yet materialized. The study concludes that industrial parks have been effective in promoting employment and improving labor market performance but have had limited success in stimulating domestic investment. The findings highlight the need for complementary policies that improve access to finance, strengthen domestic supplier linkages, facilitate technology transfer, and enhance the participation of local investors to maximize the broader economic benefits of industrial park development in Ethiopia.

detail.abstract: Repeated interaction routinely produces structure absent from the one-shot game: reputations, norms, conventions, and other institutions. The problem is to say what this structure is, when the bare game predicts play, and where the extra structure comes from. This paper argues that the institutional content of repeated play is a strict extension of the stage game: a refinement with genuinely new predictive distinctions not definable as a function of the game's own vocabulary. The argument uses a finite, fully explicit repeated-game laboratory, with mathematical claims verified by exact finite recomputation and reproducible validators, and a pre-registered re-analysis of a published human repeated Prisoner's Dilemma dataset. The institutional state studied here has a canonical form: the coarsest predictive summary of history, equivalent to a predictive-sufficiency or causal-state construction. On the finite carrier this object is non-definable from the game itself, and the predictive failure of stagevocabulary models is priced exactly by a conditional mutual information. The quantitative constants governing institutional collapse are reproducible within declared protocols but resist shortcut: across a declared formula class and three frozen out-of-sample transfer attempts, no tested low-complexity shortcut transfers across families. In the human data, the corresponding predictive-residue hypothesis is confirmed out of sample under a protocol registered before any data access, while a more specific pre-registered timing hypothesis fails in the reverse direction: history-dependence grows with experience. Claims are scoped to the declared finite carrier, declared run families and protocols, and analyzed dataset; broader framework theorems are imported and cited, not reproved here.

title: Planetary Radius as a Regime-Dependent Relational Quantity: Evidence for a Paradigm Defect in Exoplanet Radius Measurement --A Cross-Disciplinary Empirical Test in Astronomy Based on Factor Hierarchy Theory and the Four-Test Method

detail.title: Planetary Radius as a Regime-Dependent Relational Quantity: Evidence for a Paradigm Defect in Exoplanet Radius Measurement --A Cross-Disciplinary Empirical Test in Astronomy Based on Factor Hierarchy Theory and the Four-Test Method
detail.abstract: Core Conclusions: (1) Transit depth is not an intrinsic property of a planet, but a "relational quantity" arising from the coupling of the planet, the stellar radiation field, and the detector response. (2) The discovery facility is a proxy regime factor for the stellar radiation field-the true regime factors are stellar spectral type, metallicity, and surface gravity. (3) The concept of "planetary radius" as used in astronomy for four decades lacks physical universality in cross-regime comparisons. This study applies the Principle of Testability and the Four-Test Method proposed by Tang (2026g), augmented by the 5W2H and PDCA completeness frameworks, to a presupposition-free exhaustive analysis of 39,913 raw records from the NASA Exoplanet Archive. Exhaustive testing automatically selected radius_ratio + pl_orbper + sy_dist as the optimal combination from 12 candidate executing factors (adjusted R² = 0.691, VIF < 5). Interaction effect testing revealed that the discovery facility systematically modulates the exposure coefficient of radius_ratio on transit depth (ΔR² = 0.048, p = 6.59×10⁻⁷); however, this effect completely vanishes when controlling for stellar spectral type-G-type: F = 0.05, p = 0.99; K-type: F = 1.01, p = 0.39. This finding reveals a new structural form within Factor Hierarchy Theory: the proxy regime factor. Stellar spectral type, metallicity, and surface gravity were all tested and confirmed as significant regime factors. The regime coupling is strongest in the metal-poor group (ΔR² = 0.0313, p = 1.21×10⁻¹⁵) and disappears in the metal-rich group (p = 0.428). A temperature threshold of 4762 K (F = 10,283) and a surface gravity threshold of log g = 4.64 (F = 14,645) constitute a double critical point for regime switching. The number of planets observed by both Kepler and TESS is zero. Permutation tests (empirical p = 0.002), quantile regressions (all quantiles p = 0), and pseudo-out-of-sample prediction (RMSE amplification of 4.4×) comprehensively support the conclusions. This paper proposes a procedural criterion: before merging multi-facility transit data, one should conduct interaction and Chow tests 2 using candidate regime factors as grouping variables; if both are significant, the regime switch should be acknowledged, and separate modeling should be adopted rather than forced uniform calibration. Given that Factor Hierarchy Theory has independently replicated the same hierarchical structure across five financial markets and exoplanetary transit measurements, this paper proposes elevating this theory to the status of Factor Hierarchy Law. The empirical process of this paper also completes the first cross-disciplinary implementation of the 5W2H and PDCA frameworks as completeness companions to the Four-Test Method.

title: Artificial Intelligence, Strategic Communication, and Allocation

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence, Strategic Communication, and Allocation
detail.abstract: This paper studies strategic communication in allocation decisions. A receiver decides whether to allocate an object, such as a job, admission slot, grant, or contract, to an informed sender. The sender privately knows the value of the allocation and privately chooses between two communication tests: a direct test or an AI-assisted test. In equilibrium, AI-use declarations are uninformative cheap talk. AI matters instead through signal generation and the receiver's interpretation of signal realizations. The paper characterizes pure-strategy Perfect Bayesian Equilibria and, using an information-design approach, derives the equilibrium payoff correspondence as the AI-assisted test varies. Receiver credibility and sender obedience reduce the design problem to four equilibrium regions: pooled AI use, certification, imitation, and AI deterrence. If AI can only repackage information already contained in the direct test, then it cannot generate selective certification: certification requires new information, while imitation, pooling, and AI deterrence can arise from repackaging alone.

detail.abstract: Industrial parks serve as critical Special Economic Zones (SEZs) in Ethiopia, designed to promote exportoriented industrialization, attract Foreign Direct Investment (FDI), and stimulate sustainable economic growth. This study evaluates the impact of these parks on industrial performance using key macroeconomic indicators, addressing a knowledge gap regarding the actual performance of Ethiopia's rapidly expanding industrial park sector. Employing a mixed-methods research design, the authors utilized a panel dataset covering 68 zones and two federal-level city administrations. The analysis applies a Difference-inDifferences (DID) approach, comparing pretreatment (2012-2013) and post-treatment (2016-2018) periods for second-generation industrial parks. The empirical results demonstrate that industrial parks have a positive and statistically significant impact on firms' performance across multiple dimensions. Specifically, enterprises located within industrial park zones achieved significantly higher levels of working capital, investment in fixed assets, total sales value, annual production value, and total export value compared to those in control zones. These findings align with Agglomeration Theory and Export-Led Growth Theory, suggesting that the clustering of industries and shared infrastructure effectively reduce transaction costs and enhance competitiveness. The study concludes that industrial parks are effective policy instruments for promoting industrial growth in Ethiopia and recommends continued expansion alongside improvements in infrastructure and administrative efficiency.

detail.abstract: This paper identifies and characterizes a structural property, hitherto unnoted, in a class of growth models: when a firm’s accumulating factor (capital or a knowledge base) may grow without bound, but its value output enters profit only through a bounded saturating map, firm value is finite for every positive discount rate, and this finiteness is independent of the growth rate of accumulation (the level of value still depends on the path). We call this property saturation decoupling. The main theorem delivers three conclusions: (i) value is unconditionally finite, V ≤ π/ρ < ¯ ∞, even when the state diverges and even at the AK knife-edge or super-exponential growth; (ii) limρ→0 ρV = Π(x∞), the profit at the state’s long-run limit x∞ = limt x(Kt); (iii) limρ→∞ ρV = Π(x(K0)) (initial profit). The latter two are the economic incarnations of the final- and initial-value theorems of the Laplace transform, and they furnish a falsifiable characterization that is opposite to standard AK endogenous growth: in AK, ρV diverges as ρ → g +; here it stays bounded. We generalize the model to the optimalcontrol problem of a firm that chooses investment and prove (Corollary 1) that saturation decoupling survives optimization—the ceiling ¯π/ρ is independent of whether the firm optimizes—lifting the result to a genuine statement about firm value. We provide a heuristic Amdahl-type micro-foundation for saturation, a distinguishability criterion (with an explicit identification limit), and a refutable econometric specification.

However, empirical evidence on the multidimensional factors shaping the economic impact of industrial park development projects remains limited. This study examines the latent economic, social, political, technological, cultural, and environmental dimensions influencing the economic impact of industrial park development projects in Ethiopia. A mixed-methods research design was employed using survey data collected from employees, managers, administrators, and community representatives across Ethiopian industrial parks. Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) with Principal Component Analysis and Varimax rotation was used to identify the underlying latent dimensions, while Ordered Probit and Ordered Logit models were employed to estimate their effects on the indexed economic impact of industrial park development projects. title: Subsidise Labour, Not Robots: Consumer Welfare, Creative Destruction, and a Labour Super-Deduction for the AI Transition
affiliations: Khon Kaen University

detail.title: Subsidise Labour, Not Robots: Consumer Welfare, Creative Destruction, and a Labour Super-Deduction for the AI Transition
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence lowers production costs and prices, raising consumer welfare, and by reallocating resources from low-to high-productivity firms it raises aggregate productivity; but the mass layoffs it can trigger impose a demand externality and transition costs on workers. We develop a unified general-equilibrium framework that prices all of these effects and asks which policy maximises welfare. Two results organise the analysis. First, the externality and the transition friction lie on the worker margin, while the consumer-surplus and reallocation gains lie on the technology margin; by Tinbergen's rule and the targeting principle, the two require separate instruments assigned to their own margins. Second, a robot tax violates this assignment: it raises the user cost of capital, lowers the capital-labour ratio, raises prices (cutting consumer surplus by the capital share α), suppresses reallocation, andbecause its employment effect is α(1-ε)-reduces employment whenever sectoral demand is elastic. A labour subsidy, delivered through the corporate tax code as a super-deduction with effective rate s_e = τ_c(d-1)/(1-τ_c), raises employment and output together and corrects the externality without taxing the productive margin. We then prove the central result: accounting for the gross fiscal cost of the deduction, the marginal cost of public funds, and the taxes recovered and transfers avoided from sustained employment, a labour superdeduction raises welfare if and only if ΔY + ΔCS + ΔN[A_P-A_F + (1+λ)w] exceeds the net social cost of the revenue forgone. The result is robust to increasing returns, labour-market frictions, and an endogenous skill response that makes the instrument self-limiting. The welfare-maximising response to AI is therefore not anti-automation but pro-reallocation and 2 pro-human-capital: let AI cut prices and retire inefficient production, but subsidise the productive reallocation of the workers it displaces.

title: Credit Rating Agencies, Global Debt Expansion, and the Shift from Repayment Provisioning to Refinancing Capacity

detail.title: Credit Rating Agencies, Global Debt Expansion, and the Shift from Repayment Provisioning to Refinancing Capacity
detail.abstract:
This article examines whether the growing institutional power of credit rating agencies has contributed to the expansion of global debt by shifting the dominant criterion of debt acceptability from secured repayment provisioning to expected repayment capacity. The argument is not that agencies alone created contemporary indebtedness. Global debt has been shaped by financial liberalization, falling interest rates, demographic pressures, fiscal deficits, banking crises, securitization, investor demand for safe assets, and repeated public interventions during systemic shocks. The narrower claim developed here is that credit ratings have become a crucial infrastructure through which debt is made comparable, tradable, eligible, and refinanceable across borders. In that sense, the agencies are better understood as institutional multipliers of debt capacity than as mere observers of credit risk.
The core conceptual distinction is between a provisioning logic and a capacity logic. A provisioning logic asks whether future repayment has been secured today through reserves, sinking funds, escrow accounts, pledged revenues, collateral, or dedicated amortization mechanisms. A capacity logic asks whether the debtor is likely to meet its obligations when due, including by rolling over debt, maintaining market access, mobilizing future revenues, or relying on liquidity. The article argues that modern rating practice has largely privileged the second logic. This is methodologically coherent for liquid capital markets, but it weakens the disciplinary role of repayment extinction. The result is a system in which large debt stocks can remain acceptable so long as refinancing channels remain open.
The study uses a qualitative and quantitative mixed design. Conceptually, it reconstructs the analytical categories of creditworthiness, solvency, liquidity, rollover capacity, diversification, and secured repayment. Historically, it follows the rise of rating agencies from information providers in early bond markets to regulatory reference points after the institutionalization of NRSROs in 1975 and the later use of external credit assessments in prudential frameworks. Quantitatively, it relies on descriptive data from the IMF Global Debt Monitor, the OECD Global Debt Report, the Financial Crisis Inquiry Commission, the Financial Conduct Authority, the SEC, the European Banking Authority, and rating-agency methodology materials. The paper includes tables, line charts, stacked bars, histograms, a historiogram, radar charts, and a heatmap to illustrate the debt-rating nexus.
The findings are fourfold. First, global debt has risen structurally, with public and private debt together remaining above 235 percent of world GDP in 2024. Second, sovereign borrowing in advanced economies increasingly reflects rollover mechanics: OECD refinancing requirements reached roughly USD 13.5 trillion in 2025, close to 80 percent of gross borrowing. Third, the 2008 crisis showed that high ratings may validate securities whose repayment security depends more on models, tranching, and assumed diversification than on robust loss absorption. Fourth, the rating industry remains highly concentrated, giving its methodologies systemic consequences. The article concludes by proposing a Secured Repayment Index to complement conventional credit ratings and to measure a debtor's ability to pay without uninterrupted market refinancing.

detail.title: Third-Party Determination of Interim Licenses and Security Payments: A German Approach to the Huawei Framework
detail.abstract: Litigation of Standard Essential Patents (SEPs) takes place in Europe within the framework provided by the CJEU in its landmark decision Huawei v. ZTE. However, Courts in Europe are still struggling to find the best approach for the resolution of these disputes. German courts and the UPC rely on competition law and a determination of whether the parties have been willing to conclude a license. British courts focus on the setting of license terms but their approach is not entirely convincing, either. This article shows an alternative way forward based on instruments from German civil law that use third-party determination of contract terms. It combines these instruments with a preliminary calculation of a security and down-payments to provide parties with an interest-oriented way forward. The proposed third-party determination of FRAND terms is deliberately not a final determination but limited to the interim period before a final agreement. This preserves the autonomy of the parties while supporting them in the settlement process and it does not affect the right to be heard in court. Moreover, the obligation to demonstrate willingness to grant or take a license entails the necessity not to reject the other party's proposal for a third-party determination for the interim period. And in infringement proceedings it increases the pressure to negotiate constructively to reach a FRAND compliant agreement. While the method is based on German civil law, it is transferable to other legal systems and can be equally applied in the Unified Patent Court.

detail.title: Detecting Cannabis-Alcohol Substitution in Aggregate Sales Data: Statistical Power and the Limits of Small-Sample Synthetic Control
detail.abstract: Nulls are the most common outcome of studies that look at whether the legalization of cannabis substitutes for state-level alcohol sales. This paper asks if such designs could detect substitution of plausible size. I use per-capita ethanol sales and the staggered opening of cannabis retail across the United States and estimate the pooled effect with six estimators; all six return positive-signed nulls between +0.7 and +2.8 percent. Backdated placebos produce negative pseudo-effects of one to two percent when no state had legalized. I run a design-based power simulation. Under the jackknife inference the paper reports, the primary estimator's minimum detectable effect at 80 percent power is 7.2 percent; under a designcalibrated randomization test the minimum detectable effect ranges from 4.5 to 6.4 percent across estimators. Substitution effects below two to three percent are not detectable by these estimators, and a four-percent effect is detected 46 percent of the time by the primary estimator and 70 percent of the time by the most sensitive one, leaving substitution in the low single digits mostly below reach, even when such effects are still relevant for policy decisions.

title:
AI Technology and the Evolution of Supercities 
From White-Collar Density to Nodal Control under Trust Scarcity

detail.title:
AI Technology and the Evolution of Supercities 
From White-Collar Density to Nodal Control under Trust Scarcity

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This theoretical manuscript does not involve human participants, animal subjects, clinical data, interviews, surveys, or personally identifiable data. Ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a theoretical framework for understanding how artificial intelligence may reshape global supercities. Against the expectation that AI will make dense office cities obsolete, the paper argues that AI is more likely to recompose the supercity than abolish it. The central distinction is between routine cognitive production and trusted control. Routine cognitive work-drafting, summarizing, classifying, checking, coordinating, and preparing information-can become more distributed and compressed as AI adoption rises. Trusted control remains more geographically selective because high-stakes coordination still depends on certification, enforceability, liability-bearing institutions, reputational credibility, and final judgment under uncertainty. The paper formalizes this mechanism through four variables: D(α), the density return from routine cognitive concentration; T(α), trust-scarcity rent; C(α), the cost of urban concentration; and R(α), fiscal-social redundancy. It clarifies that R(α) is not a missing component of V(α), but an orthogonal redundancy condition: a city can preserve high nodal value while losing broad social and fiscal buffers. The paper argues that AI may lower D(α) while preserving or increasing T(α), producing a "thin-but-strong supercity": globally powerful in nodal control but thinner in ordinary redundancy. It also argues that AI may narrow the supercity's population-absorption channels, turning the city from a broad opportunity machine into a more selective filtering interface. The paper develops comparative cases, testable propositions, boundary conditions, and operational proxies for trust-scarcity and codifiable-trust thresholds.

title: Legal Segregation, Ethno-Religious Boundaries, and Urban Inequality in India's Disturbed Areas Act

detail.title: Legal Segregation, Ethno-Religious Boundaries, and Urban Inequality in India's Disturbed Areas Act

declarations.funderStatement: The Weiss Fund for Research in Development Economics, Institute for Humane Studies

detail.abstract: This paper studies how legal control over property transfers shapes segregation and local amenities in developing-country cities. I examine Gujarat's Disturbed Areas Act, a law requiring administrative approval for property sales in riot-affected areas, using new spatial data on designations linked to electoral rolls, housing projects, schools, and violence. Staggered event-studies show that designation targets Muslim-majority pockets in Hindu surroundings and hardens Hindu-Muslim boundaries: Hindu presence falls 5-6 percentage points and Muslim isolation rises. In heavily exposed areas, housing prices rise while school infrastructure and exam outcomes deteriorate, revealing that price growth need not reflect broad-based neighborhood improvement.

title: The Preparation Frontier: Allocating a Finite Preparation Budget in Lower-Middle-Market Transactions

detail.title: The Preparation Frontier: Allocating a Finite Preparation Budget in Lower-Middle-Market Transactions

The frameworks presented here arise from that practice. No other personal or financial relationships influenced the work.

detail.abstract: Owners of lower-middle-market businesses are routinely advised to "get ready" before a sale, and the advice is almost always a checklist: clean the financials, tidy the contracts, modernize the systems. The checklist has a hidden assumption. It treats preparation as a set of tasks to be completed rather than a budget to be allocated, and it treats every buyer as interchangeable. Neither holds. Preparation time, capital, and owner attention are bounded, typically to a window of twelve to twenty-four months, and buyers price the same business against different underwriting models. This paper introduces the Preparation Frontier, a framework that treats readiness as a constrained allocation problem. It defines return on effort as the value recovered per unit of scarce resource, evaluated against four objectives at once: the certainty of closing, the protection of the downside, alignment with the buyer most likely to pay a premium, and the preservation of strengths the business already holds. The central proposition is that a preparation program selected by return on effort dominates uniform readiness effort, and that preparation calibrated to a generic or median buyer can reduce realized value rather than raise it, because it moves the business away from the specific buyer whose model rewards it. The framework is developed as a set of testable propositions rather than a measured result. It builds on three prior Cordis Institute papers: the aggregate post-LOI gap documented in Working Paper No. 001, the buyer-archetype divergence in Working Paper No. 002, and the execution-stage compression in Working Paper No. 003.

title: The Democratic University: Why Faster Degrees Are the Next Morrill Act
affiliations: Washington State University - Department of Accounting

detail.title: The Democratic University: Why Faster Degrees Are the Next Morrill Act
detail.abstract: The debate over accelerated degrees, online education, competency-based credentials, and microcredentials is usually framed as a tension between access and quality. I want to argue that it is actually something older and more predictable: the same argument American higher education has been having since the 1850s, wearing different clothes. The Morrill Act of 1862 was met with nearly identical objections — that practical education was not real education, that the classical university's rigor depended on its exclusivity, that Senator Morrill's critics were defending something irreducible and worth protecting. They were wrong, measurably and historically. The land-grant system that emerged over their objections trained the workforce that built the American industrial economy, funded the agricultural research that fed the world, and opened higher education to constituencies the classical university had never imagined serving. The critics of this next wave of democratization — the stackable credentials, the CBE degrees, the online programs — are making the same mistake in the same vocabulary.

title: Gold and Oil in Periods of Financial Turmoil: A LSTAR GARCH Bivariate Copula Investigation
affiliations: DISEI University of Florence

detail.title: Gold and Oil in Periods of Financial Turmoil: A LSTAR GARCH Bivariate Copula Investigation
detail.abstract: We employ Logistic Smooth Transition (LSTAR) copulas with GARCH margins to investigate the transmission of dependence across major financial assets and two key benchmark commodities. Our analysis first examines the remarkably resilient role of gold as a hedging and safe-haven asset and compares its performance with that of WTI crude oil futures as an alternative strategic commodity. The proposed estimation framework provides a flexible approach to modelling time varying dependence structures, avoiding arbitrary assumptions regarding the identification of contagion episodes or the definition of extreme market movements. The superior fit of the Gaussian copula specifications suggests that gold occupies a central position in the transmission of information across financial markets. Surprisingly, however, crude oil appears to outperform gold as a risk-hedging instrument during periods of heightened uncertainty, offering more effective downside protection in crisis episodes across three major markets. Another particularly robust finding concerns the dominant role of the CBOE VIX Index as the transition variable within the LSTAR framework. International sources of financial turbulence seem to affect dependence structures primarily when transmitted through the U.S. equity market, highlighting both the pivotal role of U.S. financial markets in the global financial system and their function as a conduit through which economically relevant information is assimilated and propagated by market participants.

title: The Principal-Less Corporation: The Subtracted Principal, Corporate Attribution, and a Custodial Condition for AI-Operated Entities

detail.title: The Principal-Less Corporation: The Subtracted Principal, Corporate Attribution, and a Custodial Condition for AI-Operated Entities
detail.abstract: A companion working paper argued that the custody of operational identity could be secured without recognising electronic legal personality, by keeping the artificial agent an operator whose acts are attributed to a human principal under a custodian's supervision. On 29 May 2026 the Argentine executive submitted to Congress a draft General Companies Law whose article 14 creates the sociedad automatizada: a limited-liability company that pursues its purpose through autonomous algorithmic systems or AI agents, with no human personnel and no human owner required. President Milei defended the reform in the Financial Times, and Yuval Noah Harari and Microsoft's AI chief, Mustafa Suleyman, replied. This paper argues that such a company is best described as a subtracted principal. It keeps the form of corporate personality but removes the human will that both the common-law 'directing mind' and Argentina's own law of corporate attribution treat as personality's referent. The argument is set against the prior literature on entities without human controllers, in which Bayern showed that such an entity was already achievable through a zero-member LLC and LoPucki diagnosed its dangers; the reform's novelty lies not in possibility but in making the entity durable and statutory. The paper also meets article 14's liability rule on its own ground. Because the same reform lets the partners fix capital freely, abolishes the minimum capital and the legal reserve, and states that nominal capital is not a real guarantee to third parties, the promise that the company 'responds with its patrimony' is secured by a patrimony the reform declines to require. The remedy proposed is a custodial condition on legal personality: a designated human responsible principal who answers for supervisory fault, on the very standard the reform already applies to administrators who use AI, together with entity-level licensing conditions that include compulsory indemnity cover. A public-policy floor in the conflict of laws, calibrated to protect good-faith third parties, completes the argument.

title: The S-E-E-D Framework of System Dynamics: A Comprehensive Visual Textbook Guide
affiliations: Asia School of Business in collaboration with MIT Sloan

detail.title: The S-E-E-D Framework of System Dynamics: A Comprehensive Visual Textbook Guide
detail.abstract: Effective decision-making and learning in a world of growing dynamic complexity requires individuals to expand the boundaries of their mental models and understand how complex system structures create their behavior. System dynamics serves as a perspective, a set of conceptual tools, and a rigorous modeling method designed to enable the clear analysis of feedback structures and behaviors within complex social, physical, and corporate environments. At the core of this methodology is the foundational principle that all dynamics, regardless of their apparent scale or detailed complexity, consist of networks governed by just two distinct classes of feedback channels: positive self-reinforcing loops and negative self-correcting loops. To interpret these complex mathematical dependencies intuitively, the system dynamics lifecycles can be understood using an integrated structural paradigm known as the S-E-E-D Framework. This framework strips away complex math and demonstrates that worldly patterns are a continuous balancing act between two absolute forces: reinforcing loops that accelerate change and balancing loops that resist it. The acronym highlights the four critical feedback states: Snowball dynamics, Equilibrium constraints, Elastic time lags, and Dominance shifts.

title: A Unified Mathematical Framework for Multiagent Economic Optimization: Closed-Form Expressions of Marginalist Optimality Based on Sfecon’s Hyperbolic Descriptions of Technical Indifference (Working Paper)

detail.title: A Unified Mathematical Framework for Multiagent Economic Optimization: Closed-Form Expressions of Marginalist Optimality Based on Sfecon’s Hyperbolic Descriptions of Technical Indifference (Working Paper)
detail.abstract:
SFEcon’s representations of macroeconomic activity resemble DSGE modeling insofar as a general input-output formulation arrives at equilibrium by way of a determinant mathematical process. Impulses toward physical and financial equilibria are, however, not directed by anything having to do with matrix algebra. Rather, continuous sequences of economic states direct themselves along realistic paths toward Pareto optimality via Euler emulations representing the building-up and working-off of physical assets over time.

If stated in DSGE’s terminology, the SFEcon algorithm’s ‘objective’ would be to discover the unique distribution of physical assets required for an overall maximization value. SFEcon’s emulations always honor the ‘constraint’ of mass conservation, as dictated by the hyperbolic shapes used to describe sectors’ production and utility tradeoffs. 

This paper presents a mathematical framework for economic optimization across all agent types, including industrial sectors, households, governments, and financial intermediaries. All such sectors will be identified in terms of technical tradeoffs expressed through multi-dimensional hyperbolic surfaces.

We demonstrate that these hyperbolic functional forms provide closed-form algebraic representations of all aspects of neoclassical marginalist causality – including, most especially, inferences of the prices and values implicit in disequilibrium states, through which the economic state is efficiently guided into a unique, equifinal, equilibrium held in place by general optimality.

title: Benchmarking Carbon Emissions: Integrated Assessment Model Scenarios versus Stock-Flow Consistency
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Benchmarking Carbon Emissions: Integrated Assessment Model Scenarios versus Stock-Flow Consistency
detail.abstract: To hold governments accountable to their ostensible commitments, civil society groups need to be able to identify and quantify discrepancies between current mitigation efforts, as reflected in year to year carbon emissions, and pathways allowing for adherence to warming ceilings. We refer to this analytical function as benchmarking. The principle benchmarking procedure employed at present entails comparing ongoing mitigation measures to a set of pathways generated by integrated assessment models (IAMs) demonstrated as feasible given IAM structure and inputs and that hold radiative forcing to a targeted level. This method fails to achieve its purpose however, since the ability to generate a given pathway in a set of IAMs does not correspond to its actual feasibility. This is because IAMs are structurally overconstrained in their representation of economic processes and underconstrained in the parameter values they employ as inputs. These issues are not remediable. Moreover, IAM-generated pathways are opaque and ill-suited for accountability purposes. As an alternative approach, this paper proposes the criterion of stock-flow consistency between year to year emission reductions and a cumulative carbon budget constraint, using the simplifying assumption of equal rates of emission reduction over time and, in the general case, approaching the constraint asymptotically. Adjustments to the model are suggested to incorporate future carbon dioxide removal (CDR) options, subject to the degree of hedging (precaution) that may be invoked to diminish reliance on uncertain future CDR capabilities and the social choice of allocating negative emissions to either offsetting emission reduction obligations or reducing targeted atmospheric carbon concentration. The model can also be adjusted for differential national responsibility in emission reduction stemming from ethical and political considerations. Due to its predication on time-invariance in carbon accounting, however, the model cannot encompass either land use, land use change and forestry (LULUCF) or the role of unstable non-CO 2 greenhouse gases such as methane.

title: Murders in US Remain Very Concentrated in 2024, with the Murders in Worst 2% of Counties Remaining at their 2020 Peaks
affiliations: Crime Prevention Research Center

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.funderStatement: Crime Prevention Research Center

detail.abstract:
The worst 1% of counties (the worst 31 counties) have 20% of the population and 41% of the murders. The worst 2% of counties (63 counties) contain 30% of the population and 54% of the murders. The worst 5% of counties contain 46% of the population and account for 71% of murders. But even within those counties, the murders are very heavily concentrated in small areas within those counties. By contrast, 53% of the counties have zero murders and another 16% have just one murder. These 69% of the counties account for only 3% of all murders in the country.

This concentration of murders remains near decade-long peak levels. Between 2010 and 2014, the share of murders occurring in the worst 5% of counties fell from 71% to 69%, but it then climbed to 73% in 2020 before easing back to 71% in 2024. Much of the increase was driven by the worst 1% and 2% of counties, whose shares of murders rose sharply between 2014 and 2020 and remained historically high in 2024, even though their shares of the U.S. population changed little over time.

title: Daylight Saving Time, Lottery Stocks, and Retail Trading
affiliations: Massey University, Albany campus, Auckland University of Technology, University of Sussex and The University of Sydney - Business School

detail.title: Daylight Saving Time, Lottery Stocks, and Retail Trading
detail.abstract: We examine how the spring Daylight Saving Time (DST) transition, a shock to sleep and cognitive function that is unrelated to firm fundamentals, affects retail investors trading lottery-like stocks. Following the DST transition, we document a significant decline in abnormal trading volume and investor attention for lottery stocks, an effect driven by retail investors and concentrated in morning trading hours. This behavioral shift leads to adverse financial outcomes: retail investors incur higher transaction costs and experience significantly lower short-horizon returns on their trades in lottery stocks. Our findings provide granular, micro-level evidence linking a cognitive shock to tangible financial losses for a behaviorally biased investor class.

title: The Relationship Between Intangible Corporate Assets and Credit Risk: Applying Intangible Assets to Z-Scores

detail.title: The Relationship Between Intangible Corporate Assets and Credit Risk: Applying Intangible Assets to Z-Scores
detail.abstract: While there have been various discussions on how intangible assets impact credit risk, no consensus on this topic has been reached. This paper demonstrates that intangible assets estimated relative to a Z-score exhibit a U-shaped relationship, i.e., these assets bear an inverted U-shaped relationship with credit risk. The primary explanation for this lies in the existence of an inverted Ushaped relationship between volatility and intangible assets. This suggests that in the realm of intangible asset investment, and particularly in areas involving substantial capital outlays, there may be a shift away from high-risk, call-option-style approaches and toward demand-driven investment characterized by lower uncertainty. Furthermore, applying estimated intangible assets to the Z-score improves its accuracy as a credit risk model, suggesting that these assets serve a complementary function in the form of accounting information.

title: Defense Promotion and Industrial Development

detail.title: Defense Promotion and Industrial Development
detail.abstract: Major economies are rearming, and rearmament is itself industrial policy. I ask whether defense promotion-especially innovation policy-can drive industrial development beyond the defense sector. I synthesize evidence on supply-side instruments (including R&D tax credits and grants) and demand-side procurement, tracing each from its effects on firms' own R&D investment through innovation and productivity outcomes to spillovers beyond the recipient firm. The evidence is conditionally positive: public support more often crowds private effort in than out, but returns concentrate among particular firms, technologies, and designs, and weaken as one moves from investment to outputs and from civilian to defense settings. Defense spillovers, in particular, cannot be assumed. I draw five lessons for designing defense industrial policy that delivers broader economic returns, with the greatest weight on Europe's rearmament. The developmental promise of defense promotion is real but conditional: whether rearmament also strengthens the wider industrial economy turns on how it is designed.

detail.abstract: Even though India's fintech revolution has achieved unprecedented financial inclusion, a critical gap still emerges between systemic access and individual agency. This study investigates the "Access-Agency" gap through a cross-sectional analysis (n=110) of rural-origin blue-collar workers in Northern India, using a mixed-methods survey. The research explored the correlation between formal financial integration and conceptual literacy. Findings reveal that despite having 100% bank account access and 85.5% UPI adoption, participants lacked long-term resilience. Debt has been identified as an intergenerational obligation, and fraud may persist despite basic security adherence. Meaningful financial inclusion would require shifting from infrastructure expansion to behavioural agency, aligning cognitive understanding with structural realities of the rural workforce.

title: Wall-Clock Economics of Scale Mixture EM over Frozen LLM Features
